stories.title: LeBron James to sit out 76ers' matchup with Bucks on Saturday, first of back-to-back games
stories.summary: James is listed as out with sciatica management, addressing an issue that sidelined him for the first 14 games of last season.
stories.detailText: In an early indication of how the Philadelphia 76ers might handle LeBron James' workload this season, he will sit out Saturday's matchup with the Milwaukee Bucks. James was officially listed as out on the Sixers' injury report with low back/ sciatica management. He was originally designated as questionable on Friday, but was downgraded on Saturday afternoon. Saturday's game is the first of a back-to-back for Philadelphia, which will play the Detroit Pistons on Sunday to close out their three-game homestand. Sciatica was an issue early last season for James, who missed the Los Angeles Lakers' first 14 games . While that hasn't appeared to be a concern for the 41-year-old through the preseason and first two regular-season contests, the Sixers apparently want to make sure that his back and legs don't become a greater problem. James averaged 33 minutes in Philadelphia's first two games, which is around the amount head coach Nick Nurse said he wanted to play him and center Joel Embiid during the early stages of the schedule. LeBron's first dunk at home 👑 The Philly crowd was HYPED 🔥 pic.twitter.com/mu0YYHkVVU — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) October 23, 2026 In two games, James is averaging 15.5 points, while leading the 76ers with 9.5 rebounds and 6 assists per contest. He's appeared to be content with being more of a facilitator and helping the Sixers on the boards, while Tyrese Maxey (30 ppg) and Jaylen Brown (20 ppg) handle the scoring responsibilities and Embiid works inside. James will apparently sit out Saturday while Embiid could miss Sunday's game. The 7-footer indicated after Thursday's 114-106 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers that he was told he wouldn't play both games of the back-to-back. He averaged 34 minutes in the Sixers' first two games. "I'm not playing both games," Embiid said, via NBC Sports Philadelphia . "I'm playing one of them. I don't know. They're going to tell me. But I feel good. Whatever they tell me, I'll do it." Philadelphia could also be without Dean Wade for the third consecutive game because of an ankle injury. Wade, 29, is listed as questionable for Saturday and has not yet played this season after spraining his left ankle in the team's final preseason game.

stories.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg doubles down on jawing with Luka Dončić: 'He's not Michael Jordan'
stories.summary: Lendeborg conceded that he might have gone overboard with his postgame comments, but he's not budging on his on-court trash talk.
stories.detailText: Golden State Warriors rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg has heard the backlash he's received from NBA fans who disagreed with him going at Los Angeles Lakers superstar guard Luka Dončić during the teams' season opener on Wednesday. Some have harped on the viral clip of Dončić telling Lendeborg amid the 127-105 Lakers victory, "Hey, bro, you're 24 and a rookie. Relax." Lendeborg dismissed that chatter, especially that belabored line. "The 24-year-old rookie thing? I'm 24 in the NBA with the best job in the world," Lendeborg told reporters Friday after the Warriors' 111-108 defeat to the Memphis Grizzlies. "Just moved my mom out to California. I'm living the dream." Lendeborg, who starred for a national title-winning Michigan team last season after playing JUCO ball and then turning more heads at UAB , explained that he's always going to be himself because that's the way he was raised. In that same postgame interview, he also doubled down on his jawing with Dončić. "He's going to say what he want to say. I'm going to say what I want to say," Lendeborg noted, via ESPN's Anthony Slater . "I'm not afraid to talk to nobody, man. He's not Michael Jordan. Come on now. It's fun trash talk. I feel like I did kind of take it overboard in the media, but, I mean, it is what it is." Here is some Yaxel Lendeborg postgame On the backlash to Luka comments: “I’m not afraid to talk to nobody. He’s not Michael Jordan.” He did admit: “I feel like I did kinda take it overboard in the media, but it is what it is.” On the Boozer matchup: “I always want to have a… pic.twitter.com/sPvnUt5eX5 — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) October 24, 2026 Dončić isn't Jordan; however, the 27-year-old Slovenian is an international icon. He's a six-time All-NBA first-teamer and a two-time league scoring champion. That clearly doesn't faze Lendeborg, whose unfiltered commentary added to his intrigue during his meteoric rise at Michigan. Lendeborg said he told Dončić 'he sucks' In Wednesday's season opener, Lendeborg didn't back down from the challenge of guarding Dončić. Even though Dončić piled up 23 first-half points, only two of those came against Lendeborg, according to ESPN tracking , which had Dončić shooting 0 of 4 from the field with Lendeborg as his primary defender in the halfcourt over the opening two quarters. Lendeborg and Dončić went back and forth throughout the contest, trading jabs amid the verbal sparring. Notably, Lendeborg was assessed a technical foul , just before Dončić banked in a buzzer-beating prayer at the end of the first half. After the game, Lendeborg said he told Dončić "he sucks." Lendeborg also said that he "lost all respect" for Dončić after seeing firsthand how Dončić plays. Lendeborg put Dončić on blast for "complaining" over the course of the game. Dončić conveyed postgame that the chirping took his performance to another level. Warriors are on board with Lendeborg's bravado While some in the basketball world have taken issue with Lendeborg's brazen approach, he's received backing from his teammates and head coach Steve Kerr in recent days. Kerr actually said on Thursday that he loves it. "But Steph [Curry] had the perfect comment," Kerr said, via Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle . "He loved it, too, but he said, 'Now you got to back it up.' And that's right. The way you back it up is to not get lured into that next week when we play them again or against somebody else who's doing that. "You'd much rather rein a guy in than have to kick him in the butt. And, so, I love Yaxel's competitiveness. He's shown that he's going to be a headache for [Warriors senior vice president of communications] Raymond Ridder all year because he's willing to say anything. But I want guys to be themselves as long as they're using that wisely to help us win basketball games." Steve Kerr, of course, saw Yaxel Lendeborg’s postgame comments on Luka Doncic. “I love it. I think the bravado, not backing down, it’s great.” He talked to Lendeborg about it, but not to scold him. “Hell yeah, but don’t foul him next time … back up your words.” pic.twitter.com/j3tM0hrCKx — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) October 22, 2026 Kerr did admit, though, that Lendeborg's Wednesday night comments "became too individual." "It's still about the team, and we got our ass kicked," Kerr said on Thursday, via Evans. "So it should be about us giving up 127 points. It doesn't matter what Luka shot against him or what the individual matchup was. We gave up 127, and we have to be better." Draymond Green, long one of the most outspoken players in the NBA, unsurprisingly has lauded his new Warriors teammate for the way he handled the testy night against Dončić. "I respect the hell out of Yaxel for being willing to stand toe-to-toe," Green said on his podcast this week. "If you can't rock with a guy like that, who compete like that, who willing to fight like that, you're probably a loser. Because if you can't get behind that, all the people are going, 'Oh man, he shouldn't be talking.' Why shouldn't he? That's like this old adage of like, 'Oh, you're a rookie, you don't talk.' F*** that. Why wouldn't I talk? The guy you criticize is the guy that does that and then tuck his tail and run. That's the guy who should be criticized, not the guy who do it, stand 10 toes on it and continues to go forward." Lendeborg offers tame remarks about latest showdown with Grizzlies' Cameron Boozer Even though Lendeborg reinforced his stance toward Dončić on Friday, his postgame media session with reporters in the locker room showcased an additional side of the authentic, do-it-all forward. Following his latest head-to-head with draft classmate Cameron Boozer, whom Lendeborg lost to last season while Boozer was at Duke and then beat in July to win an NBA Summer League title, Lendeborg gave credit where credit was due. "He played a great game today," Lendeborg said of Boozer, via Slater . "We both were on the bad end with the turnovers, but we both [got our] first double-doubles. ... First career double-doubles for both of us. It was a fun matchup. Didn't really get to guard each other much. He took advantage of his matchup when I was on him. Did a great job." Lendeborg was the 11th overall pick in this year's draft. Boozer went eight picks before him at No. 3 overall. Lendeborg expressed after winning that Summer League championship that he thinks about revenge every time he plays Boozer. On Friday, Lendeborg maintained that he looks for an edge against his draft classmates, except he freely acknowledged that Boozer outperformed him that day.

stories.title: 4 free agent centers the Suns could target after Oso’s injury
stories.summary: With Mark Williams sidelined and Oso Ighodaro injured, the Suns may need another reliable body at center.
stories.detailText: MACAO, CHINA - OCTOBER 11: Dwight Powell #7 of the Dallas Mavericks plays defense during the game against the Houston Rockets as part of 2026 NBA China Games on October 11, 2026 in Macao, China at Venetian Arena. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Following the re-signing of Mark William s, the center position felt like one of the few areas where the Phoenix Suns possessed legitimate depth, and with it, a developmental buffer. You had Williams, an experienced starting center who also carried a lengthy injury history. With him in the starting lineup, third-year center Oso Ighodaro could comfortably slot in behind him on the depth chart. And with Williams likely missing time, whether due to injury or scheduled rest (especially on the second night of back-to-backs), second-year big man Khaman Maluach would also have opportunities to get some reps. There was no need to rush Maluach’s development. The Suns could bring him along on their own timeline, allowing him to grow at a pace they felt was appropriate. But the news that Williams would miss a significant amount of time following surgery to repair a torn labrum in his shoulder changed that equation. Suddenly, Maluach’s developmental timeline accelerated, and the overall depth of the Phoenix Suns at center took a substantial hit. Now, one game into the regular season, that depth is already being tested. Per Suns insider Duane Rankin, Oso Ighodaro will be out Saturday night against the Golden State Warriors with an oblique injury. Suns coach Jordan Ott said Oso Ighodaro will miss Saturday's game as he was diagnosed with an oblique strain. When asked if the injury is related to the hip, Ott said he's not a doctor. Added Luke Kennard (knee) practiced today, trending in right direction. #Suns — Duane Rankin (@DuaneRankin) October 23, 2026 Ighodaro exited Wednesday’s season opener against the Portland Trail Blazers before the conclusion of the first half and did not return. With confirmation that he’ll miss Saturday’s game, the question becomes how much additional time he might be sidelined. Oblique injuries can be particularly difficult to navigate, as is the case with many injuries that affect movement on the basketball court. Look at Orlando’s Paolo Banchero, who suffered an oblique injury early in the 2024–25 season. His initial recovery timeline was six weeks, but he ultimately returned 11 weeks later. There are three varying grades of oblique injuries: Severity Grade Typical Recovery & Absence Timeline Grade 1 (Mild Strain) 1 to 3 weeks (approx. 11.6 days) Grade 2 (Moderate Strain) 3 to 6 weeks (or up to 6–8 weeks depending on depth) Grade 3 (Severe / Full Tear) 6 to 8+ weeks (sometimes requiring surgical evaluation) We don’t yet know the severity of Ighodaro’s injury, but the circumstances certainly provide cause for concern. If he misses any significant amount of time, the team is in quite a pickle. Right now, the Suns’ center room consists of Khaman Maluach and newly acquired two-way players Duop Reath and Drew Timme. That’s it. However, following the decision to waive Haywood Highsmith before the start of the regular season, Phoenix has one open roster spot. They could go shopping on the market for assistance, given that they have $4.4 million of flexibility under the second apron (which they are hard-capped at). Who is out there? Let’s look. Dwight Powell I’ll start with 35-year-old Dwight Powell, who brings 13 years of NBA experience, nearly all of it with the Dallas Mavericks. Across 768 career games, primarily in a backup role, Powell has averaged 6.5 points and 4.2 rebounds. He’s not going to stretch the floor, as he’s a career 29.4% three-point shooter, but he did post a career-high 15.1% rebounding percentage last season with Dallas. And the Suns? They could use some of that rebounding. This doesn’t project to be a dominating rebounding team, and quite frankly, you’ll need all of the assistance you can get. The Mavericks waived Powell this offseason after giving him an Exhibit 10 opportunity to stay with the team as they pivot toward prioritizing youth at center, making him an option who could provide Phoenix with much-needed depth and rebounding off the bench. His rim protection would be welcomed, as his overall defensive talent is rated in the 83rd percentile by B-Ball Index, with an A- grade. From Mavs Moneyball ’s Ben Zajdel on Dwight Powell last season: Having a player like Powell around can help. A player who’s seen everything, has a personality that’s uplifting, and is generally a good hang can keep a bad season from turning into a disaster. Things in Dallas could have turned toxic quickly this year, and for the most part, the team was drama-free. Powell was a part of that, and it’s something NBA teams value. Kelly Olynyk If you want to talk about players with a high motor who would fit the culture Phoenix is trying to establish, you’d be hard-pressed to find somebody who fits that profile better than Kelly Olynyk. Olyknk has made a career out of being a hustle player, the shot of energy off of the bench that might not put up statistical dominance, but affects those around him with his motor. His 13-year career has spanned eight franchises, most recently with the San Antonio Spurs, where he appeared in 42 games as a backup last season. Throughout his career, Olynyk has averaged 9.8 points and 5 rebounds, and he can knock down the occasional three-pointer as well, shooting 36.9% from deep on 3 attempts per game. While his athleticism has begun to decline with age, at 7 feet tall and 240 pounds, Olynyk brings size, experience, and an established work ethic that could serve the Suns well given their current circumstances. He’s not as analytically effective as Dwight Powell, but he is someone who can assist in crashing the boards (you see a theme here for me? Johnny wants rebounds), especially on the offensive end. If he’s your second-team center, extra opportunities would be appreciated. Bismack Biyombo What am I doing here? Just looking at all of the backup bigs the Spurs let go this offseason? Well, yeah. They had a trio of veterans behind Wemby and opted to move on. And since the Suns are in a bind, we could use them. I’m normally not big on retreads, but when you look at the list of available centers, you’re bound to come across a few former members of the Phoenix Suns. Mason Plumlee is available (another former Spur), as is Drew Eubanks. But if I were picking somebody from that pile, it would be Bismack Biyombo. We know him from his two seasons in Phoenix, where he appeared in 97 games, starting 17, and averaged 4.9 points and 4.4 rebounds. We also know he can’t space the floor in any capacity, and his push shot leaves plenty to be desired. But if you need somebody who can come off the bench and provide a physical presence on the glass, even at 6-foot-8, Biyombo is capable of doing exactly that. After all, he averaged 10.8 rebounds per 36 minutes and possesses a career rebounding percentage of 16.7%. I wouldn’t mind having him back around, knowing that his impact is primarily one-dimensional. Jonas Valanciunas The last guy on my list might be the most intriguing, and that’s 15-year veteran big man Jonas Valancuinas. The Big V who has bounced all over the NBA but never into the Valley of the Sun. If you’re looking for a big body, this is your guy. At 6’11” and 265 pounds, Valanciunas brings a physical presence and a skill set that could help the Suns in several areas. He can knock down a midrange jumper, finish around the basket, and isn’t afraid to get his hands dirty fighting for rebounds. After all, across 14 NBA seasons, he’s averaged 12.8 points and 9.0 rebounds. His rebounding percentage? 20.7%! The Suns are a team that certainly lacks size, and Valanciunas provides exactly that. He ranks in the 7th percentile for defensive rebounding talent but in the 94th percentile for offensive rebounding talent. He’s strictly an interior player at this stage of his career. He can’t defend the perimeter effectively, nor can he stretch the floor offensively. But if rebounding is a priority, which I firmly believe it should be for this team, Valančiūnas is somebody the Suns should absolutely pursue. Big V is currently playing in the EuroLeague for Zalgiris in the Lithuanian Basketball League, playing in his home country on a two-year, $5.5 million contract. The Rest Here’s a list of everybody else who is available on the free agent market: Tony Bradley Drew Eubanks Christian Koloko Kevin Love Josh Oduro Lachlan Olbrich Mason Plumlee Olivier Sarr Oscar Tshiebwe My guess is that the Suns will ultimately lean on Duop Reath and Drew Timme as they await further clarity on the severity of Oso Ighodaro’s injury. But the flexibility is there if they decide to explore other options. What do you think? Should the Suns stand pat? Or, after just one game into the new season, should they go out and add some much needed flexbility.

stories.title: Mavericks' Cooper Flagg out for home opener with mild left shoulder sprain
stories.summary: Mavericks star forward Cooper Flagg had an MRI that revealed a mild left shoulder sprain, the team announced. He will not play against the Spurs.
stories.detailText: DALLAS -- Mavericks star forward Cooper Flagg had an MRI on Saturday morning that revealed a mild left shoulder sprain, the team announced. Flagg has been ruled out of Saturday night's home opener against the San Antonio Spurs . He will be reevaluated next week. The reigning Rookie of the Year, Flagg suffered the injury when he took a flagrant foul by Indiana Pacers forward Aaron Nesmith on a breakaway late in the second quarter of the Mavericks' road win Friday night. Flagg exited moments later and did not return to the game. Flagg, 19, was off to a fast start in his second season. He scored 32 points in Wednesday's loss to the Houston Rockets , the highest-scoring performance ever by a teenager in a season opener. He had 14 points, six assists, five rebounds, three steals and a block in 17 minutes before exiting against the Pacers.

stories.title: Magic's Paolo Banchero has ankle sprain; out multiple weeks, sources say
stories.summary: Magic star Paolo Banchero has sustained a low-grade high ankle sprain, the team announced, with sources telling ESPN that the forward will miss multiple weeks.
stories.detailText: Orlando Magic star Paolo Banchero has sustained a low-grade high ankle sprain, the team announced Saturday, with sources telling ESPN's Shams Charania that the forward will miss multiple weeks. This injury diagnosis typically carries a timetable of four to six weeks. Banchero was injured in the first half of Friday night's 115-93 loss to the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves . He told The Orlando Sentinel after the game that he began experiencing discomfort in the first quarter. He sat out the fourth quarter and finished with 14 points and six rebounds. Last season, the Magic outscored opponents by 45 points in the 182 minutes that Banchero, Franz Wagner , Jalen Suggs , Desmond Bane and Wendell Carter Jr. were on the court together. They collectively shot 50.1% from the field and 36.4% from 3-point range while holding opponents to 46.2% overall shooting and 34.5% 3-point shooting. The Magic are 40-26 over the past three regular seasons when the quartet of Banchero, Wagner, Suggs and Carter all play. They went 7-3 in 10 games without Banchero last season. Over the past two seasons combined, Banchero has missed 46 games, Wagner 70 and Suggs 72, yet the Magic still reached the playoffs both years. Banchero was off to a flying start this season, averaging team highs of 24.5 points and 7.5 assists per game, along with 6.5 rebounds and doing all that on 70% shooting. For his career, the 2022 No. 1 draft pick and 2024 All-Star is averaging 22.4 points, 7.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game for Orlando. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.title: 76ers' LeBron James to sit vs. Bucks in first game of back-to-back
stories.summary: LeBron James will miss the Sixers' game against the Bucks to manage low back pain/sciatica. It will be his first missed game of the season.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- LeBron James will miss Saturday night's game against the Bucks to manage low back pain/sciatica, the 76ers announced. Saturday marks the start of Philadelphia's first back-to-back; they play the Detroit Pistons on Sunday, also at home. James missed the opening 14 games of last season with sciatica, which is the irritation of a nerve that runs through the gluteal muscles, hamstrings, lower leg and foot. James, 41, hasn't said publicly that he has had any injury flare-ups this season. As his injury designation suggests, this appears to be managing the past injury over a long season for the NBA's oldest player. After two games this season, James is averaging 15.5 points and leads the 76ers in rebounds (9.5) and assists (6.0) per game. Forward Dean Wade , who has yet to make his Sixers debut while nursing a left ankle sprain, remains questionable.

stories.title: Magic's Paolo Banchero suffers high ankle sprain in loss to Timberwolves, reportedly could be out 4-6 weeks
stories.summary: Banchero left Friday night's loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves early.
stories.detailText: The Orlando Magic need a spell to lift their injury curse. They've been haunted by ailments, the latest of which reportedly could sideline their best player for more than a month. Magic star Paolo Banchero is now nursing a low-grade right high ankle sprain, the team announced Saturday . The injury, according to ESPN's Shams Charania , usually comes with a four-to-six-week recovery timeline. Banchero, a 23-year-old one-time All-Star forward, exited a 115-93 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves in the third quarter Friday night and didn't return. Banchero sustained the injury in the first half, per the team. He finished with 14 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists in a setback that dropped the Magic to 0-2 in the infancy of Sean Sweeney's first season at the helm . Paolo Banchero underwent an MRI, which has confirmed a low-grade right high ankle sprain. Banchero suffered the injury during the first half of last night’s game vs. Minnesota. He will undergo further testing and evaluation, and his status will be updated as appropriate. pic.twitter.com/lkrP9SvyAC — Orlando Magic (@OrlandoMagic) October 24, 2026 During the Magic's season-opening defeat to the Atlanta Hawks, Banchero piled up 35 points on 10-of-12 shooting, plus 10 assists and 7 rebounds. The Duke product, whom Orlando selected No. 1 overall in the 2022 draft, is coming off a 2025-26 campaign that saw him average 22.2 points, 8.4 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game. He helped the Magic reach the playoffs for the third consecutive season, except they were once again bounced in the first round. Orlando blew a 3-1 lead to the top-seeded Detroit Pistons, leading to the firing of Jamahl Mosley, who's now the head coach of the New Orleans Pelicans. Just before that coaching change, in the fallout of the Magic's collapse, Banchero admitted his group wasn't "good enough" at the time to make the Eastern Conference finals or NBA Finals. Due to the Magic's injury woes, it's been difficult for them to realize their potential. Now, just two games into Sweeney's stint, Banchero is sidelined. Last season, Banchero, Franz Wagner, Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane and Wendell Carter Jr. were all on the floor together for just 182 minutes, according to ESPN , which also reported that, during that small sample size, the Magic outscored opponents by 45 points. Banchero missed 36 games in 2024-25. Suggs wasn't on the court for 47 games that season. Wagner was out for 48 games last season and then notably wasn't available for the final three games of the first-round series versus the Pistons .

stories.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg accomplishes feat not seen in decades in home debut
stories.summary: Afterward, the former Michigan star was wearing a throwback Warriors jersey he dug out of his closet. Let's just say it fit the occasion.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO — An hour or so after the Warriors’ collapse Friday night, Yaxel Lendeborg stood at his locker and swapped out his white No. 1 jersey for a blue throwback No. 4. Dug out of his childhood closet by his mom, it was already an appropriate homage for a Michigan man trading in one shade of blue for another. Then, Lendeborg went on to have a game that no Warriors rookie had had since the guy whose name was on the back of that jersey. “This is the jersey I’ve been wearing since I was a kid on the basketball court,” Lendeborg told reporters in the locker room following Golden State’s 111-108 loss to the Grizzlies . “Chris Webber, Michigan legend. Warrior legend. Had to represent, you know?” Golden State Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg (1) dunks the ball during a game against the Memphis Grizzlies at Chase Center in San Francisco, Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Lendeborg did more than represent. Although he got the short end of his first NBA showdown with fellow rookie forward Cameron Boozer, Lendeborg matched the No. 3 overall pick with 13 rebounds and six assists to go with 18 points — the first Warriors rookie since Webber to put up such a line in one game. Only two Warriors, period, in the past six seasons have stuffed the stat sheet to the degree that Lendeborg did in just his second professional game. Steph Curry went for 23, 13 and 13 back in 2021. And Brandin Podziemski notched 18, 15 and nine this past February. That’s it. However, Lendeborg was also responsible for six of the Warriors’ 19 turnovers. “He’s gonna get better and better,” coach Steve Kerr said. “He just has to get used to the NBA. … He’s putting himself in some risky spots that he won’t be doing a few weeks from now.” Yaxel Lendeborg (1) of the Golden State Warriors smiles against the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday, October 23, 2026, at Chase Center in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images Yaxel Lendeborg (1) of the Golden State Warriors and Cameron Boozer (27) of the Memphis Grizzlies battle during a game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images After going back and forth with Luka Doncic in his NBA debut, Lendeborg kept it more lowkey in his first game in front of the home fans. He said this summer that he would have any matchup with Boozer, whose Duke team he beat for the national championship, circled on his calendar. “I always want to have a good game against anybody in my draft class, try to outperform them. Today I didn’t,” Lendeborg said. “But every game I’m definitely gonna try to take that personally, try to win my matchup and ultimately win the game for the team. “I didn’t do both today, but I’ll win it next time.” Boozer operated at will and finished with 25 points, seven more than Lendeborg — one off the difference in their draft positions. His spinning shot in the lane over Podziemski with 20 seconds left gave the Grizzlies their first lead since late in the third quarter, 108-106. Lendeborg, meanwhile, is still seeking his first NBA win. “He played a great game today,” Lendeborg said. “It was a fun matchup. Didn’t really get to guard each other much. He took advantage of the matchup when I was on him and did a great job. Props to him.” Download The California Post App, follow us on social, and subscribe to our newsletters California Post News : Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , X , YouTube , WhatsApp , LinkedIn California Post Sports Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , YouTube , X California Post Opinion California Post Newsletters : Sign up here! stories.title: Jayson Tatum claims ‘there’s no beef’ with Jaylen Brown after trade: ‘Ain’t no f–king Shaq and Kobe’
stories.summary: Jayson Tatum explained where his relationship with former teammate Jaylen Brown stands.
stories.detailText: tatum brown Jayson Tatum explained where his relationship with former teammate Jaylen Brown stands. “I don’t have any animosity or beef or ill will toward him,” Tatum said after the Celtics’ 107-103 win over the Knicks on Friday. “The frustrating part is, since he’s not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or conversations haven’t been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning the championship, how we’ve grown together, right?” Tatum’s comments on his relationship with Brown stem from a social media interaction between the two superstars earlier in the week. Brown posted a blue hat — a symbol for “cap,” the slang definition of someone telling a lie — in an Instagram comment section to a video of Tatum saying on his YouTube channel that he was “just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world” by Brown’s trade to the 76ers this summer. Jayson Tatum of the Boston Celtics takes a shot against Mikal Bridges #25 of the New York Knicks during the Celtics home opener at TD Garden on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, in Boston. Getty Images Brown and Tatum spent the previous eight seasons together in Boston. Brown was drafted by the Celtics in 2016, and Tatum was selected a year later in 2017. The wing duo won a championship together in 2024 against the Mavericks, with Brown earning Finals MVP, and also made it to the NBA Finals in 2022 — along with five conference finals appearances. The two were able to combine for eight All-Star appearances and five All-NBA selections during their time in Boston. “This ain’t no f–king Shaq and Kobe,” Tatum said, referring to the issues between Hall of Fame teammates Shaquille O’Neal and the late Kobe Bryant that occurred during their eight years together on the Lakers. “There’s no beef. It’s not about that. It should be more praise. I understand drama gets clicks and views, but I’m not really into that. I’m not blaming everybody for how they feel. Everybody is entitled to their own feelings, and we all go through different things in our lives.” The first matchup between the two will be on Nov. 10 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia. Jaylen Brown of the Philadelphia 76ers celebrates during a game against the New York Knicks on Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, at Madison Square Garden in New York. NBAE via Getty Images Jayson Tatum was talking about the Jaylen Brown trade and Brown went in the comments and called him a LIAR. This NBA season gonna be CRAZY pic.twitter.com/AGUJ6WDp0Y — Hater Report (@HaterReport) October 23, 2026 “I’ve seen all these things about ‘Get your popcorn ready when they play’ — like this ain’t no f–king boxing match, it’s basketball,” Tatum said. “I hate the conversation, the narrative around it. There’s not enough communication, and a conversation will solve or put out a lot of fires.” Tatum’s 36 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in Friday’s win marked his best performance since Game 4 of the Eastern Conference semifinals two years ago against the Knicks. Jayson Tatum (0) and Paul George (13) of the Boston Celtics box out during a game against the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit. NBAE via Getty Images He scored 42 before rupturing his right Achilles, an injury that forced him to miss most of last season. With Tatum on the sidelines, Brown carried the Celtics to 56 wins and the second seed in the East. Tatum returned for the final 16 regular-season contests and played in six games in Boston’s first-round series against Philadelphia, missing Game 7 with a left knee injury. The Celtics lost the series after building a 3-1 lead.

stories.title: Warriors implode late as Grizzlies' 17-0 run caps stunning comeback
stories.summary: The Warriors appeared to be in control before "pretty much everything went wrong" in the final four minutes, when the Grizzlies rallied from 12 down to win 111-108.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO -- In his second career NBA game, No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer capped a 17-0 run and a stunning 111-108 comeback win for the young Memphis Grizzlies with a nine-foot floater in the closing seconds Friday night against the Golden State Warriors . Three minutes earlier, the Warriors were in control. Veteran wing De'Anthony Melton made a corner 3 with 3:47 left to put them up by 12, appearing to seal an uplifting home win two nights after an embarrassing road loss to the Los Angeles Lakers to open the regular season. "Eight different things had to happen," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said of the late collapse. "If any one of those eight doesn't happen, I think we win. It was just an avalanche." Stephen Curry made the initial mistake. The 18-year franchise legend was overzealous on a closeout in the corner and fouled Memphis guard Jaylen Wells on a made 3, giving the Grizzlies four quick points to resuscitate hope. Curry, Draymond Green , Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski then combined to miss four consecutive shots over the next 80 seconds, any of which might have slammed the door on the Grizzlies. "Pretty much everything went wrong," Curry said. That's when Boozer took control. He powered through fellow rookie Lendeborg and Melton on back-to-back possessions, earning and hitting four free throws. Ty Jerome , the NBA's leading scorer with 73 points through two games, drilled a corner 3 after a loose-ball scramble with 1:24 left to pull the Grizzlies within one. Wells hit a free throw with 54.7 seconds left to tie it. That set the stage for Boozer, who finished with 25 points, 13 rebounds and six assists. After a Curry miss with 35 seconds left, Boozer was being defended by the significantly smaller Podziemski and attacked with a controlled drive and spin into the floater range. Boozer turned and swished the nine-footer to give the Grizzlies the 108-106 lead. The Warriors never had a legitimate opportunity to tie it. On the ensuing possession, Green was called for setting an illegal screen near half court. Kerr was so upset with the call that he yelled at the officials and received a technical. "We probably had six illegal screens tonight," Kerr said. "The flopping that was happening on every single one, it looked like guys were going down like they had been hit by a car." The Grizzlies made three free throws, including the technical on Kerr, completing a 17-0 run to flip the game in the final four minutes. That was the second-longest fourth-quarter run by an opponent in the Kerr era, according to ESPN Research, behind only a 21-0 run by the Houston Rockets in 2018. "There are losses," Curry said, shaking his head. "Then there are losses like tonight that sting a little bit more." Friday's loss was particularly painful for a depleted Warriors team attempting to tread water long enough in the first two months to get Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody , their injured starting wings, back in the lineup. "We didn't close the game," Kerr said. "It didn't happen. It's a long season. We will win our share of those games as well." The Warriors travel to Phoenix for a back-to-back set Saturday night and are expected to be without the resting Curry, who said he "probably" won't play, and Podziemski, who said he will miss the game while managing back soreness.

stories.title: Lakers guard showered with praise for raising team’s defensive energy
stories.summary: The Lakers got an immediate boost from one of their guards making his season debut.
stories.detailText: For Matisse Thybulle, one of the “coolest” things about this current Lakers team has been having “so many defensive-minded players”. The types of players who’ll stack a hustle play on top of another play, creating an advantage and energy for the team as a whole. That’s how the veteran wing saw things play out during the Lakers’ win over the Clippers on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. Collin Sexton (10) made an immediate impact for the Lakers with his defense. NBAE via Getty Images Lakers guard Collin Sexton (10) “invigorated the game with more energy,” as Matisse Thybulle put it after the team’s win over the Clippers on Friday. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill And he credited Collin Sexton, who made his Lakers debut during the victory , with providing the team with that jolt. “I felt like it immediately,” Thybulle said. “He just invigorated the game with more energy.” Sexton’s first minutes of the season after sitting out the preseason and the regular-season opening win over the Warriors on Wednesday came when he subbed in for Austin Reaves with 3:52 left in the first quarter. Eleven seconds later, the veteran guard stripped Clippers guard Darius Garland of the ball during his drive into the paint, leading to a steal for the Lakers after Luka Doncic dove on the floor to corral the ball. “He’s a pest,” Reaves said. “He feeds off the energy, he loves doing the little things and plays the game the right way. He’ll have a big impact [on] what we’re trying to do.” The former Alabama guard carried that energy into the second quarter. The Lakers value Collin Sexton’s intensity. NBAE via Getty Images “He has a really intense way about him that I think will be really good for our group and guys will feed off that,” coach JJ Redick said. With the Lakers down 44-38 early in the quarter, his perimeter defensive pressure against Kris Dunn forced the Clippers to eat up 10 seconds of the shot clock before Dunn passed the ball to rookie guard Keaton Wagler. Wagler tried forcing a pass to Brook Lopez on the low block while Ziaire Williams was in front of him, but the ball floated over the 7-foot-1 center’s head and Reaves grabbed the steal. But the errant Clippers’ possession started with Sexton hounding Dunn even though he didn’t get credited in the box score for the play. In addition to his three steals, the 6-foot-3 guard also had five points and two assists in 16 minutes. “Ziaire and I talk about it a lot: That’s what we try to do for them,” Thybulle said. “Even as people who try to do that, to see someone else doing it, it gives us even more energy. It’s just one of those things that when everyone else is doing it, you don’t want to be the guy to not be. It’s almost like when you’re working out in practice and like everyone’s making shots in a row, you don’t want to be the one to miss it and mess it up. Defensively, you can have a similar thing, which is effort and energy.” Sexton brought an abundance of both in the Lakers’ second win of the season. stories.title: Walker Kessler is exactly who the Lakers needed
stories.summary: Looks like the Lakers got their franchise center. They needed a bastion down low. They listened to Luka Dončić when he said he wanted Walker Kessler. Rob Pelinka gambled everything...
stories.detailText: Looks like the Lakers got their franchise center. They needed a bastion down low. They listened to Luka Dončić when he said he wanted Walker Kessler. Rob Pelinka gambled everything to get him. In his first two games? Kessler is making Doncic look like a skilled scout. And he’s making Pelinka look like a man with good job security. Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler, left, shoots as LA Clippers center Brook Lopez defends during the second half of an NBA basketball game Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill The 7-foot-1 center, whom the Lakers acquired over the summer in a sign-and-trade deal with the Jazz , had 22 points on 10-for-14 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists, six blocked shots and three steals in the Lakers’ 125-117 win over the Clippers on Friday. He had the highest plus-minus (+18) of anyone on the court. That followed a 26-point performance on 12-for-12 shooting, nine rebounds, one assist and two blocked shots in his regular-season Laker debut against the Warriors on Wednesday. This is who the Lakers wanted. This is who they needed. This is who could turn them into contenders. Everyone knew the Lakers’ offense was going to be incredible behind Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. But last season, the Lakers ranked 20th in defensive efficiency. They desperately needed to improve. So, the Lakers gave the Jazz two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to acquire the 25-year-old Kessler, signing him to a four-year, $130 million deal. It was a risk. It meant they wouldn’t have any tradable first-round draft picks for the next seven years. It meant Kessler would make or break this Laker team. So far, so great. In his debut against the Warriors, he was the first Laker since Wilt Chamberlain to shoot 12-for-12 in a game. And against the Clippers, he became the eighth Laker to record six blocks and three steals in a game, according to Stathead. “He’s a fantastic basketball player and I think he’ll continue to get better,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. “I mean, that was one of the reasons that we wanted him and he was so appealing to us was because of his age and feeling like the fit with our two stars was really good. And [he’s] someone that can continue to grow and become just a fantastic player in the NBA.” LA Clippers guard Kris Dunn, left, drives toward the basket as Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler defends during the second half of an NBA basketball game Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Kessler only played in five games last season after suffering a torn left labrum that required surgery. After missing an entire season of his prime, there were a lot of questions . What’s his ceiling? Is he going to live up to expectations? Was he really worth the enormous price the Lakers paid for him? Memories are short in the NBA, especially when a player misses 77 games. But Kessler is silencing his doubters. “Oh, it’s so much fun,” Kessler said of being back on the court. “It’s so much fun. It was definitely a tougher year for me. But God is faithful. And just to be here now, I’m just so thankful. So thankful for this opportunity. So thankful to be healthy. Just very, very thankful.” The Lakers need Kessler to develop into an All-Defensive-type player. They need him to complete their Big 3 alongside Doncic and Reaves. They need him to be a force. He’s checking those boxes. After the score was knotted at 64-64 at halftime, Kessler took over in the third quarter with his defense, helping the Lakers lead by as much as 14 points in the period. “It just felt like Walker was everywhere in that third,” Redick said. “…There were multiple times [in the game] where it felt like they had a layup and he either came over and blocked the shot or created an altered shot.” Kessler’s next game will meld his future with his past as the Lakers travel to Utah to face the Jazz. For Kessler, it’s a return to where he spent the first four seasons of his career. “I’m so excited to compete against those guys,” he said. “Coach [Will] Hardy does a great job with that franchise and my past teammates are really talented, really competitive. So I think it’s going to be a very competitive game and I’m just excited to go compete.” But for the Lakers, it’s a reminder of how far they’ve come. They emptied their treasure trove for Kessler. And so far, every pick they gave Utah was worth who they got in return. stories.title: Lakers open up about former forward: ‘One of my favorite teammates’
stories.summary: The Lakers were happy to have Rui Hachimura back at Crypto.com Arena.
stories.detailText: It isn’t often that Lakers superstar Luka Doncic will joke around with an opponent – especially during a game. His recent verbal back and forth with Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg throughout the Lakers’ season-opening win on Wednesday night showcased a glimpse of how competitive the Slovenian guard can get on the court. But Doncic was especially exuberant during the Lakers’ win over the Clippers on Friday night because the game was also Rui Hachimura’s return to Crypto.com Arena after the Japanese forward spent 3 ½ seasons with the Lakers, which included 1 ½ as a teammate with Doncic. Austin Reaves and Rui Hachimura were Lakers teammates from 2023-26. NBAE via Getty Images Luka Doncic was being jovial with Rui Hachimura throughout Friday. NBAE via Getty Images Doncic ran onto the court and hugged Hachimura pregame before the Clippers forward could start his routine. And even when the 2019 first-round draft pick was going through his pregame process, there Doncic was, being jovial with his former teammate as Hachimura greeted his old Lakers coaches. The playfulness from Doncic’s side continued during the game. “I don’t like Rui…Nah, it was just great to see him,” Doncic said. “He’s my guy. We had a year and a half together, great friends, so it was really nice to see him.” The playfulness turned into trash talk when the game started. “He was just trying to talk trash or whatever,” Hachimura said. “But I don’t care about that stuff. I had a good time with him, two years with the Lakers. I’m happy to see him.” It was clear Doncic wasn’t the only Laker who was happy to see Hachimura. Hachimura and Lakers star guard Austin Reaves, who were teammates during the former Gonzaga forward’s entire tenure with the Lakers, also embraced on the court pregame and postgame on Friday. Clippers forward Rui Hachimura was all smiles during his return to Crypto.com Arena. NBAE via Getty Images “He’s one of my favorite teammates I’ve ever had,” Reaves said. “I made a joke the other day that I didn’t know if he spoke English for the first two weeks. We sat by each other on the plane his first year and I would say hey to him. He kind of just looked at me and [nodded]. “And then after that I couldn’t get him to shut up. Always in a good mood, happy to be here, puts the work in and it’s just good to see him be happy and successful and enjoying his life.” Hachimura’s demeanor is why coach JJ Redick said he was “one of my favorite players I’ve ever been around in the NBA.” “One of my favorite players I’ve ever coached,” he added. “And it’s because of just the consistency of joy and personality that he brings every day.” And that joy radiated from Hachimura throughout Friday, despite his new team losing to his old team. He finished with 16 points, six rebounds and two steals in 33 minutes against the Lakers. “It was amazing, it was a great time with them,” Hachimura said of his time with the Lakers. “This organization, of course I missed them. But it was time to move on. It was special, my four years, four seasons with them. I’m happy with the Clippers right now. I gotta keep going with my career.” Download The California Post App, follow us on social, and subscribe to our newsletters California Post News : Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , X , YouTube , WhatsApp , LinkedIn California Post Sports Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , YouTube , X California Post Opinion California Post Newsletters : Sign up here! stories.title: Inside the Suns: Game 1, the next 11 games, Drew Timme, Oso’s contract extension
stories.summary: Your weekly Inside the Suns analysis straight from the BSotS community who live and breathe the team.
stories.detailText: Welcome to Inside the Suns, a deep-down analysis of the current Phoenix Suns team in which the Fantable — a round table of Bright Siders — give their takes on the Suns’ latest issues and news. Fantable Questions of the Week Q1: What stood out to you in the Suns’ first regular season game against the Trail Blazers? zenzino: Whew! Glad that one is out of the way. The Suns got pulled under in the Portland wave and never resurfaced. To call out any specific players for that game is asinine. That level of suck was a total team effort. There were no bright spots. The Blazers threw a ‘welcome home Dame ’ three-point party, and the Suns were the wallflowers. That being said, we learned nothing from the first game. But the second game will tell us plenty about who they are going to be. Will they bounce back with effort? Will they lock down on defense? Will they hit a shot in the first 6 minutes? What’s done is done. They still have the same number of losses as the Knicks and the Spurs (as of this writing). The next game is a lot more important than the last one. Notable: Koa Peat made his NBA debut in the season opener, scored his first points, and got his first tech/fine. Welcome to the NBA. Ashton: Next question. Pass. I literally asked Rod to strike this question in the game chat to save you all and me the mental anguish of having to relive it. I was denied. Planet Orange? More like Clockwork Orange. I knew this question was coming, but I felt like I was strapped in a chair, unable to blink or turn away from the train wreck that I saw and is now permanently imprinted into my memories as I watched it from start to finish. Now, let’s get to the positives and negatives. Positives: Literally none. If I had to call one positive out it was the over-600 post-game chat where we were unified in our negativity, and it was more entertaining than the actual game. Negatives: Oh, where to start? How much time do you have? Sorry, I have to make an appointment with my sports psychologist. This team is a work in progress, and that is putting it lightly. OldAz: I was out of town on business and had been maneuvering all day to find a place to watch the game. As meetings ran long, the game started while I was with some associates at dinner, and I stuck to following the start of the game on my phone. Let’s just say I didn’t have much motivation to find someplace to watch the rest of the game by the time dinner was over. I guess I did not spend much time paying attention to the other moves around the league this offseason, as I can understand why Portland came out with high energy and excitement. Their backcourt of Ja and a healthy Dame, with Jrue and Scoot coming off the bench! Plus, their best player is still probably Avdija, with some nice pieces along the front line. My impression is that Game 1 is a small sample size and more a product of a really good team centered around defense that is primed to break out this season. As for the Suns, that’s an ugly way to start, but I won’t draw too many conclusions around 1 game. Rod: Nothing good. At this point, I have no idea as to whether it was one of those games where basically everything just goes wrong or many of us had some very unrealistically high expectations for this team. I mostly believe it was the former, but I’m quite eager for the next game to get a sign as to whether the 1st game was an aberration or the new norm. There’s a saying from boxing that basically says that everyone has a plan…until they get hit. Well, the Suns got smacked around hard in the 1st quarter in Portland, and everything pretty much fell apart from there on. I can only hope that’s not the new team identity for 2026-27. Q2: The Suns’ schedule starts off with 9 of their first 12 games at home. What are your thoughts on this? zenzino: Hopefully, it will help them get off to a good start. However, I’m not a fan of the easier home schedule to start because, as we’ve seen in the past several seasons, that usually means a really tough schedule down the stretch. Last season in particular, they had a legit shot at the 6th seed, but their last 10 games were mostly away and against some top teams. Ashton: That Suns fans may actually set decibel level records for booing if they see the same effort that the Suns put against Portland at home against GSW. Heck, they may even set off seismic monitors around the Valley. The conversation may very well trend towards the over/under on how many points the Suns will get beat by. Is it 20 or 30 or even worse? Because what I saw on the road against Portland did not seem like it would translate into a home-court advantage. There is just too much to fix. Now, granted, I am submitting this on a Friday and keeping the Cardinal Rule of my game emotions in check for at least 24 hours after a loss. I failed. GSW did not exactly look like world-beaters in their loss to the Lakers. Let’s see how that one turns out on Saturday. Maybe my tune will change when it comes to home-court advantage. OldAz: Those 12 games are a big sample size, so they better get their defense in order quickly. A lot of home games should allow for time to work on their deficiencies with less travel to deal with. Otherwise, things could get ugly fast. There are not many easy opponents in the Western Conference, so not a lot of room for an extended slow start. Rod: After the Game 1 debacle, all I can think of to say here is, “It can’t hurt.” Perhaps playing in front of the home crowd will give them a little additional motivation to get their act together, and hopefully keep it together, once they get out on lengthy road trips. In 11 days, the Suns will face off against the Blazers again, but in Phoenix this time. How well they perform in that game is of particular interest to me. Q3: What is your opinion of the addition of Drew Timme to the Suns on a two-way contract? zenzino: Like most people, Timme wasn’t high on my name recognition list. From everything I’ve read and seen since, it looks like he’s a less athletic version of Oso. Connector, team defender, good passer. He has a post-up game but is not quite as good a ball-handler. No outside shot. Not particularly good at rebounding. I didn’t check his free-throw percentage, but I’m just going to assume it’s better than Oso. Makes me wonder if they knew Oso’s hip was going to be an on-off problem this season. Still no word about that at this writing. It’s a 2-way contract. There is only possible upside. CG was a 3rd-year 2-way signing, and look how that turned out. Ashton: I grew up in a small town outside of Spokane, and I love what Mark Few has done to prepare his players for the NBA at the collegiate level. Heck, the University of Arizona took his best assistant for head coach and that has turned out pretty well. I consider Gonzaga my second favorite team in college basketball and probably the last mid-market collegiate titan dynasty in the NIL era. Now, with that said, the track record of Gonzaga players succeeding in the NBA has been spotty. I could go through the list (also RIP Brandon Clarke), but I won’t. Quite a few of them were hyped in mocks and actual NBA draft selections. Andrew Timme was voted as a consensus All-American at the collegiate level three times and remains Gonzaga leading scorer. His reward? He went undrafted in 2023. Any Phish fans on the board? My favorite song is “Bouncing Around the Room”. This is Timme’s career in a nutshell because he has bounced around on two-ways, G League, and NBA contracts on multiple teams. Six of them, to be exact, before picking up his seventh team with the Suns. So, I do not have the answer to this question. I do not think anyone does. But I liked watching him play at Gonzaga, thus my focus on college play. Timme is worth a flyer. OldAz: Don’t know much about him, but I was never overly enamored with Brea, so I am glad they prioritized more front court help with their remaining two-way spots. In the past couple of years, Gregory has found good value in this pool of players, so hopefully he has done so again. Rod: I think he’s a good addition, especially in light of Oso’s hip injury. Timme’s listed as a power forward, but he’s spent most of his time on the court playing center over his first two seasons (79%). At 6’9″, he’s a bit small to play at the 5, but he’s pretty much the same size as Reath (but 10 pounds lighter). I expect that’s where he’ll most likely get some court time with the Suns this season if Oso’s hip injury turns into a lingering issue. Unlike Oso, Timme can actually shoot from three (33.3% career, 44.0% last season on limited attempts), although he hasn’t played enough to know just how much you can count on him hitting those frequently. As an emergency backup, I’m happy with adding him to the roster. Bonus Q: Do you like or dislike Oso Ighodaro’s contract extension? zenzino: I’m thrilled! Another team-friendly deal that also makes the player happy. Total win-win. He played all 82 games last season for a reason. Even when MW was healthy and playing well, more often than not, Oso was out there at the end of the 4th quarter. Even if a lot of people here don’t think he is all that great, the coaching staff and his teammates have a lot of confidence in him, and they showed it when they locked him up for the next 4 seasons. Thrilled, I tell you! Ashton: Wait. A bonus question that suspiciously seems like a Q4. Fantable, we need to unite and unionize against the three-question format turning into four questions or more! What is next, five questions? I checked our Fantable CBA (we don’t have one), and it specifically states that all opinions presented by Fantable are free of charge and allowed to be changed by the editors. Furthermore, any content provided by Fantable can be pilfered by the writers for roundtable and article discussions. To the question. I liked the contract terms. There was a run on back-up centers (that is what Oso is) at the NBA trade deadline. This will happen again as NIL deals for collegiate centers are at an all-time high, and they will return for the money. The days of drafting a center on the cheap are probably gone. Also, Lakers overpay for center Walker Kessler is looking good, but we will see how it ages. So yes, a good value for Oso. With that said, I am more than a little concerned about Oso’s hip injuries to start the season. I hope the trainers are not pushing him out while not 100 percent healthy. Yes, the center position is a need for the Suns, but let’s not rush it. OldAz: I think it was good value and don’t really correlate his contract to the hip injury, as he has been pretty healthy during his career. However, for this season, their lack of depth at center, with his hip injury added on, does not bode well at all. This next week could get rough if that lingers. Rod: I’ve seen some fans call it an overpay, but I think it’s about right for a quality backup center today. Yes, Oso has some faults/limitations, but so do all backups at every position…or they wouldn’t be backups (with a few rare exceptions). As always, many thanks to our Fantable members for all their extra effort this week! Quote of the Week “This (the loss to Portland) is definitely a wake-up call for us. I’m glad it happened early. Everything went wrong. We have a lot to learn from the tape offensively and defensively.” — Devin Booker Suns Trivia/History On October 25, 1975, Phoenix Suns Ring of Honor member Alvan Adams made his NBA debut for the Phoenix Suns in an 89-88 win over the Portland Trail Blazers. He was just 2 assists short of getting a triple-double (14 points, 10 rebounds, 8 assists) in his NBA debut. Adams also played a big role in helping the Suns get to their first-ever NBA Finals appearance, where they were defeated 4-2 by the Boston Celtics. stories.title: Ex-NBA player Malik Beasley negotiating plea deal in gambling case
stories.summary: Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with Department of Justice lawyers over his alleged role in a bribery and betting scheme, one of his attorneys confirmed.
stories.detailText: Former NBA player Malik Beasley is negotiating a plea agreement with Department of Justice lawyers over his alleged role in a bribery and betting scheme, one of his attorneys confirmed Saturday. An overnight notice on the court docket indicated that Beasley, who played for six NBA teams over a nine-year career, intends to plead guilty in the case. Attorney Steve Haney told ESPN in a text message that Beasley has not signed a plea deal with prosecutors but that talks are ongoing and a decision is expected early this week. A spokesperson for the Eastern District of New York did not immediately reply to follow-up questions about the matter. Prosecutors allege that Beasley, 29, deliberately manipulated his statistics in at least four games during the 2023-24 season while he was with the Milwaukee Bucks so that gamblers could place and win bets on his performances. According to the indictment, his co-defendants selected games that would not be nationally televised and Beasley decided whether he would underperform or overperform his scoring and rebounding. Though he had earned tens of millions of dollars during his career, Beasley also accumulated "multimillion-dollar gambling losses" when he became part of the alleged scheme, according to the indictment. Beasley faces federal counts of bribery in sporting contests, wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy. He initially pleaded not guilty to all of the charges. Late Friday, however, the judge overseeing his case asked a federal magistrate in Brooklyn to schedule a hearing for Beasley to change his plea. The judge filed a similar order Friday for another defendant in the case, Ernesto Plascencia. Plascencia's attorney confirmed Saturday morning that he will be entering a guilty plea. One of the other defendants in the case, William Brown, pleaded guilty earlier this month, while fellow sports bettor Robert Gorodetsky is slated to formally enter a guilty plea Nov. 20. Former NBA player Ed Davis and Paolo Zamorano, who was Davis' agent, were also charged in the case and have pleaded not guilty. ABC News contributed to this report.

stories.title: Key Lakers vs Clippers takeaways: Kessler's hot start has LA cruising
stories.summary: The Lakers earned a 125-117 victory over the Clippers in the first game of the crosstown rivalry season series at Crypto.com Arena on Friday, Oct. 23.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Lakers beat the L.A. Clippers 125-117 in the first game of the crosstown rivalry series at Crypto.com Arena on Friday, Oct. 23. Austin Reaves nearly had a double-double for the Lakers with 28 points and nine assists. He finished 10-for-13 shooting from the field and 5-for-6 from the free-throw line on the night. Luka Doncic added 23 points, seven assists, and six rebounds for the Lakers but also turned the ball over 11 times. The Lakers ran away with the game in the third quarter, outscoring the Clippers 39-26. Darius Garland nearly matched Reaves’ production, finishing with 26 points and six assists for the Clippers. The Lakers improve to 2-0 to start the season and will travel to play the Utah Jazz on Sunday. The Clippers fall to 1-1 and will look to rebound against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday. Walker Kessler continues to have early success Walker Kessler has not disappointed through his first two games in a Lakers uniform. The Lakers’ new big man had an efficient night, going 10-for-14 (71%) from the field against the Clippers' defense. He finished with 22 points and eight rebounds in 35 minutes of play. The center also showed up on the other end, coming up with a game-high six blocks. Kessler was coming off a strong debut with the Lakers, having scored 26 points and collected nine rebounds in 30 minutes of play against the Golden State Warriors on Oct. 21. He went 12-for-12 from the field. More: Walker Kessler delivers big opening night statement in Lakers debut Lakers’ defense a proven strength Kessler was responsible for six of the nine total blocks that the Lakers recorded on the evening. Kessler and Collin Sexton each had three steals while three other players had at least two steals for the team. The Lakers finished with 13 total steals. Clippers struggle to keep the ball Garland followed up his strong start to the season with another 25+ point performance but was also responsible for nine of the team’s 26 turnovers. The Clippers finished the first quarter with a 31-27 lead but had eight of their turnovers come during that period. The team had allowed just nine total turnovers in the first half against the Sacramento Kings earlier in the week. Coach Tyronn Lue’s team fell apart in the third quarter after giving up 13 turnovers. Rui Hachimura’s return spoiled by Lakers Hachimura returned to Crypto.com Arena for the first time since joining the Clippers this past offseason. Hachimura had 16 points and six rebounds in 33 minutes of play. He shot 5-for-14 from the field. Hachimura was seen reuniting with his former teammates, such as Doncic, before the game. He was also seen pretending to go back to the Lakers’ locker room as he had for four seasons before joining the Clippers as a free agent. "It was amazing. It was a great time with them," Hachimura said after the game on Friday. "Of course I missed them, but it was time to move on. "It was special, my four years, four seasons with them. I'm happy with the Clippers. It's my eighth year; it's a really big year for me. I'm focused on that." More: Rui Hachimura looking forward to playing on other side of Lakers-Clippers rivalry Brook Lopez turns back clock Center Brook Lopez helped lead the Clippers in the first half against the Lakers. In the first half, Lopez came off the bench for eight minutes and produced 15 points on 6-for-6 shooting and 2-for-2 from the 3-point line for the Clippers. He did go 1-for-2 from the free-throw line. The game was tied at 64. More: Veteran Brook Lopez producing strong start to season for Clippers Lopez finished with 22 points and four rebounds. He went 8-for-9 from the field and 4-for-5 from the free-throw line. The 38-year-old began his 19th season in the NBA with a double-double off the bench on Wednesday against the Sacramento Kings. He produced 17 points with 10 of his 11 rebounds coming on defense. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Key Lakers vs Clippers takeaways: Kessler's hot start has LA cruising

Mikal Bridges as Knicks lose in Boston 107-103: 0 points 0-8 shooting 0-5 three 0 free throws pic.twitter.com/8AdLsvxlfw — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 24, 2026 Mike Brown On the Knicks’ slow start and still figuring out the team’s identity: “I haven’t even looked at 50 wins, or 45 or 52 or anything like that. I’m still trying to figure out this team a little bit. I know everybody is like, ‘Whoa, it’s the same team as last year. New season, new team, new challenges, and so I’m not even sure who I wanna play yet, you know? Trying to figure the little things out.” On Mikal Bridges’ shooting struggles against the Celtics: “Mikal had three or four wide-open 3s. And obviously we want him to make half of them if they’re open. But he’s got to keep shooting. And hopefully they’ll eventually go in — sooner than later. But he’s getting the looks that he needs to get. He just has to knock them down now. And he’s got to make sure he’s physical on the defensive end.” On Bridges and the Knicks needing to play more physically on defense: “He’s got to make sure that he’s physical on the defensive end. And he, as well as everybody else because it was all of us, are laying on screens when we get hit, and that when we do switch, there’s a level of physicality to the switch so that they’re not able to take advantage of us.” On what went wrong for the Knicks in the 107-103 loss to Boston: “It was a physical ball game, and we have to give Boston credit. They had the advantage with the physicality.” On Jayson Tatum’s 36-point performance against the Knicks: “Jayson Tatum did what Jayson Tatum does. You just take your hat off and say, ‘Good D, better O.’ But that’s not why we lost the game. We lost the game because we didn’t handle their physicality on both ends of the floor for too many stretches that were too long.” Knicks start season 0-2 First time since Leon Rose's first full season in charge 6 years ago Next up: Orlando in the Garden Sunday evening pic.twitter.com/gxxtyCbVz5 — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 24, 2026 Jalen Brunson On the Knicks’ progress despite starting the season with two losses: “I think we took a stride, just not big enough strides. There’s positives and negatives to take from this game. We know what we have to do, and the things I think are glaring to us are controllable. So that’s a positive we can take from this.” On how the Celtics helped shape the Knicks into a championship team: “The way they were playing, and I guess how they’re still playing, kind of helped shape our team. They were obviously a dynamic force. And obviously the past couple years with injuries and personnel changes and stuff like that, things are different. We were trying to figure out how we can beat those guys.” On Mitchell Robinson not watching the Knicks’ championship ring ceremony: “We know Mitch is a competitor. He’s a person who wears his emotions on his sleeve … that’s just Mitch being Mitch.” On Robinson leaving the Knicks for the Celtics: “It’s definitely bittersweet. He’s a good friend. I’m just happy he was able to get a nice payday.” Josh Hart + Boston = hit in face pic.twitter.com/UcLhLgWqPt — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 24, 2026 Josh Hart On having limited involvement in The Roommates Show’s Polymarket sponsorship agreement: “To be honest, we really don’t have much of a say in terms of a lot of the sales and who they reach out to. I don’t wanna say we know nothing, but we don’t know much about all that stuff. “I know they sit there and talk about, it’s trading; it’s not gambling.” On being surprised by the controversy surrounding the Polymarket sponsorship: “Last year, we had BetMGM. I don’t really know too much around the controversy of it or whatever. I saw some things on Twitter, and I was just like, ‘Oh, I didn’t know people felt that way.’ “I saw a little bit of it the last couple days, and I was shocked — and it might be a little ignorance on my part because I don’t know, but yeah.” On taking advantage of sponsorship deals to pay the pod employees more: “When it’s the pod and that, I kind of play ball a little bit because there’s other people depending on that. So it gets brought to us at the very end and for me personally, I’m just like other people are depending on this. So I play ball with that.” Deuce to Mitch: “My dawg 4l” Mitch to Deuce: “My bro 🩶” pic.twitter.com/QdF3ZzZnkI — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 24, 2026 Mitchell Robinson On the Knicks’ locker room without him: “I know it ain’t no fun no more. I know. I just brought so much light to this team.” On feeling unwanted by the Knicks during free agency: “They didn’t want me? Yeah. That’s what it felt like. I was like, cool. There wasn’t bad blood behind it. Man, fresh start.” On signing with the Celtics despite their rivalry with the Knicks: “The only thing that was kind of different was going to the rivals. But you know me, man. I like to troll. Nobody was happy with that move. But I was.” On learning to treat the NBA as a business after years of trade rumors: “Anything can happen, I can be traded at any moment. I was in so many of those trade talks. I’m like, ‘I just got to see it as a business. You can’t let your feelings in it.’ That’s kind of what I did.” On his understanding of the NBA’s second-apron salary cap restrictions amid his Knicks exit: “Not too much. But it is what it is.” On having a more active offensive role with the Celtics: “I’m a lot more active. Constantly moving on the offensive end. It’s actually going pretty great. I got to bring the energy.” NEWS: The Knicks say using the allure of rings for a cybersecurity test was "an unfortunate mistake." They reveal plan to hand out 275 championship rings worth over $3.7 million. Story here: https://t.co/dW5HJ8FCxZ — Stefan Bondy (@SbondyNBA) October 23, 2026 Knicks Rep On using a championship-ring bait in an employee phishing simulation: “The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers. MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack. Using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake.” On the narrative about the Knicks’ wrongdoing: “There is a great deal of misinformation regarding the championship rings. The plan has always been to distribute more than 275 rings and jewelry to the people in the organization who were part of last season’s success. As is common with many teams, the players were always supposed to get their rings as part of the opening night ceremony and then everyone else will receive theirs in about 4-6 weeks. Regarding the phishing email, the process of securing and reminding our employees to protect our IP was not a mistake but the choice to use the ring to do so was a mistake and we apologize to our employees and the fans. “Winning the championship was a great moment for all New Yorkers. Those who choose to focus on the negative are missing the joy that comes with the team’s accomplishment.” Knicks fans named their baby “Knickson Fyve” 🥹🔥 (via knicksonfyve/ig) pic.twitter.com/Q4m2SYU6kF — Complex Sports (@ComplexSports) October 22, 2026

stories.summary: Toronto secures its first road win over Washington with Dybansta sidelined

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Stephen Gosling/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Toronto Raptors improved to 2-0 on the season after defeating the Washington Wizards 112-102 at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. It marks Toronto’s first 2-0 start since 2019, the season the franchise won its first NBA championship. While the final score may suggest a convincing win, the Raptors’ performance was far from perfect. Inconsistent three-point shooting, communication issues and fouls remain areas for improvement as they look to build on this result in their upcoming games. Scottie Barnes led the way with an impressive double-double, recording 28 points and 14 rebounds. RJ Barrett also delivered a strong performance, finishing with 23 points and nine rebounds, while Kawhi Leonard contributed 16 points and eight rebounds. Both teams came out looking to establish their perimeter game, with the first five shots of the contest all coming from beyond the arc. After the early attempts went unanswered, RJ Barrett connected from three-point range to get Toronto on the board, before Kawhi Leonard followed with a three of his own on the Raptors’ next possession. Toronto continued to look for opportunities from deep, attempting eight three-pointers within the opening minutes of the game. Their offence remained productive thanks to contributions from across the lineup. The Raptors defensive intensity helped set the tone throughout the quarter, limiting Washington’s key offensive contributors and making it difficult for the hosts to establish a rhythm. A scoring run from the bench, led by Ja’Kobe Walter, Jamal Shead and Allen Graves, helped the Raptors extend their advantage. Toronto closed the quarter with a 34-21 lead, establishing early control of the game. However, six turnovers in the opening frame highlighted the need for better decision-making in transition and improved communication moving forward. The second quarter opened with both teams trading baskets as the Wizards began to find their rhythm offensively. Toronto’s communication continued to be an issue, as Trae Young knocked down back to back wide open three pointers to cut the lead to eight, forcing Darko Rajaković to call a timeout. However, the sloppy play persisted, allowing Washington to gradually chip away at the advantage. Foul trouble also became a concern, with Kawhi Leonard, Immanuel Quickley and Colin Murray-Boyles each picking up their third personal foul. The Raptors eventually settled down, with a timely scoring run from Ja’Kobe Walter, Scottie Barnes and Leonard helping rebuild their lead to 13 late in the quarter. Anthony Davis began to find his footing after a relatively quiet first half, scoring late to bring Washington back within single digits. It was far from a convincing first half for Toronto, but the Raptors did enough to take a 60-52 lead into the break. WASHINGTON, DC – OCTOBER 23: Kawhi Leonard #2 of the Toronto Raptors dribbles the ball during the game against the Washington Wizards on October 23, 2026 at Capital One Arena in Washington, DC. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Stephen Gosling/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Toronto’s struggles carried over into the third quarter, as continued fouls and miscommunication allowed the Wizards to cut the lead to three. The Raptors’ offence, which had looked disjointed throughout the night, eventually found some momentum through Immanuel Quickley, Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett, helping rebuild a six-point advantage. Washington continued to respond with baskets of its own, but Jamal Shead provided a spark for Toronto, playing a key role in a run that extended the lead to 10 as the Wizards began to get sloppy. However, Washington answered with an 11-2 run late in the quarter to close the gap once again. Toronto’s three-point shooting remained a major concern, going just 1-of-12 from beyond the arc in the frame, with Jamison Battle finally connecting from deep with 12 seconds remaining. The Raptors entered the fourth quarter clinging to an 81-77 lead. Quickley gave the Raptors an early spark in the fourth, converting a tough floater through contact to extend the lead to six. Leonard followed with a three-pointer, while Barnes also found the basket, providing encouraging signs for a Toronto offence that had struggled to find consistency throughout the night.
