(Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Scottie Barnes continued to make his presence felt on both sides of the court, but the hosts refused to go down without a fight, knocking down back to back three pointers to keep the pressure on Toronto. Barnes briefly appeared to be dealing with a knee issue, holding his knee before making his way to the bench under his own power. After a short spell on the sidelines, he returned to the game late in the frame. Despite the Wizards’ late push, Toronto did enough to close out the contest, securing the victory. The Raptors were shown a much tougher battle against the Wizards and they can expect another test on Sunday as they travel to Minnesota to face the Timberwolves. Tip-off is set for 7pm.

stories.title: Milwaukee Bucks vs. Philadelphia 76ers Preview & Game Thread: David vs. Goliath?
stories.summary: On the second night of a back-to-back, the Bucks have an opportunity to make major noise. Get ya slings out!
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 27: Tyrese Maxey #0 of the Philadelphia 76ers dribbles the ball against Ryan Rollins #13 of the Milwaukee Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena on January 27, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s SEGABABA time for the first time in 2026-27! Yes, the day after playing their home opener, the Milwaukee Bucks travel to Pennsylvania to take on LeBron James and the star-studded Philadelphia 76ers. Yesterday, the Bucks lost a close one to the Chicago Bulls in a showing that offered plenty of promise, but also raised some red flags—namely, point of attack defence and ball security. Tonight, against a much tougher opponent, can the Bucks step up and win one for the little guys? The Task Ahead These aren’t your father’s 76ers—and they certainly aren’t the 76ers of recent years either. No, after acquiring five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown and 22-time All-Star LeBron James to pair with seven-time All-Star Joel Embiid and two-time All-Star Tyrese Maxey, these 76ers are quite legitimately an All-Star lineup. Next to them in the starting lineup is 2025-26 All-Rookie team selection VJ Edgecombe. Yeah, these guys are stacked . But as history has shown over and over again—see the Durant/Harden/Irving Nets, the Kobe/Gasol/Howard/Nash Lakers, and the Shaq/Kobe/Malone/Payton Lakers—putting a troupe of All-Stars together doesn’t automatically mean they’ll run away with the league. So, are these 76ers any good? Thus far, the answer is yes. The 76ers are undefeated in the young season, beating the reigning-champion New York Knicks 106-100 on Opening Night and the Eastern Conference-finalist Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 on Friday. And they’ve been doing it while shooting poorly. Over the two contests, Philadelphia is shooting just 44% from the field and a paltry 27% from deep, but all that star power has helped them get to the free throw line a whopping 28.5 times per game (a number that would’ve ranked first in the league last year). Milwaukee’s task is to therefore defend without fouling. They struggled with this against the Washington Wizards, conceding 41 attempts, with Anthony Davis and Trae Young combining for 30 of those. While the Bulls don’t present star power akin to those two—and certainly not compared to the 76ers—2025-26 All-Star Norman Powell did have seven first-half free throws on his way to nine for the game yesterday and the Bulls took 30 altogether. Injury Report Bucks : Not yet submitted. 76ers: LeBron James: Questionable ( old low back/sciatica) Dominick Barlow: Out (low back stress reaction) Tacko Fall: Out (left quadriceps strain) Ariel Hukporti: Out (right Achilles tendon rupture) Player to Watch Despite being the fourth-biggest name on his own squad, Tyrese Maxey is quickly emerging as the 76ers’ best player. It’s fitting too, dude is grease lightning. A blur across the hardwood and even quicker with the trigger, Maxey has gotten off to a blistering start this season, averaging 30.0 PPG, 5.5 APG, and 2.5 SPG thus far. What’s more, he’s averaging 15.0 PPG in the paint . With the Bucks struggling defensively at the point of attack and at the rim, giving up 65.0 PPG in the paint so far, don’t be surprised if Maxey ups those numbers in this one. Ryan Rollins, what ya got? stories.title: Dalton Knecht lands with the New York Knicks on a two-way deal
stories.summary: A fresh start for Dalton.
stories.detailText: Tennessee guard Dalton Knecht (3) reacts after hitting a three-point shot during an NCAA college basketball game between Tennessee and Kentucky in Knoxville, Tenn., Saturday, March 9, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Dalton Knecht’s frustrating time with the Los Angeles Lakers has come to an end. The team waived Knecht earlier this week, finally freeing the former Tennessee Volunteer to explore better opportunities. On Friday, he found one with the defending NBA champions. Knecht signed a two-way contract with the New York Knicks, according to multiple reports. The two-way deal will allow Knecht to go back and forth from the Knicks to the team’s G-League affiliate. Former Lakers forward Dalton Knecht has agreed to sign with the New York Knicks on a two-way NBA contract, his agents at Excel Sports Management tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/1gePugMy3Z — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 23, 2026 Knecht averaged 7.1 points per game during his time with the Lakers, appearing in 132 games. He made 16 starts during his rookie season, where he averaged over nine points per game. Knecht shot 36.8 percent from three point range during his two seasons. Somewhere along the way, Knecht fell out of favor with the Lakers and struggled to find the floor. The Lakers had a trade in place to move Knecht to Charlotte, but the deal fell through after center Mark Williams failed his physical. Los Angeles ended up waiving Knecht 20 months later. At Tennessee, Knecht put up one of the most prolific offensive seasons we’ve ever seen. The fifth-year senior transferred in from Northern Colorado and averaged 21.7 points per game while shooting over 39 percent from three-point range. Knecht took over several games for Tennessee down the stretch, helping push the Volunteers to another Elite Eight appearance. Knecht now lands in New York, where he’ll wear No. 99 for the Knicks. We’ll see if he can find new life, now finally with a fresh start.

stories.title: Sixers-Bucks by the numbers: New faces, paint points and opposite halves
stories.summary: Milwaukee’s new core has supplied most of its scoring, but its first two opponents have done their damage inside and at the foul line
stories.detailText: Sixers-Bucks by the numbers: New faces, paint points and opposite halves originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Bucks team visiting Philadelphia on Saturday night does not look much like the one the Sixers have grown accustomed to facing. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis are in Miami. Four former Heat players have entered Milwaukee’s rotation. Taylor Jenkins has replaced Doc Rivers as head coach, and the Bucks have opened the season with losses to the Wizards and Bulls. The Sixers, who will be without LeBron James , will begin a back-to-back Saturday. Milwaukee will complete one at Xfinity Mobile Arena after playing its home opener Friday night. Two games are not enough to establish what the Bucks will be this season. They have provided a few numbers worth knowing before the Sixers attempt to improve to 3-0. 139 Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel’el Ware and Kasparas Jakučionis have combined for 139 of Milwaukee’s 241 points. The four players acquired from Miami in the Antetokounmpo trade have accounted for 57.7 percent of Milwaukee’s scoring. By comparison, Philadelphia’s offseason additions have scored 45 percent of the Sixers’ points. Herro has scored 58 points. Jaquez has added 41, while Jakučionis and Ware have combined for 40 off the bench. Herro and Jaquez have started both games alongside Ryan Rollins, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner. Jakučionis and Ware have been regular members of Jenkins’ rotation. Herro has led Milwaukee in scoring and assists. Jaquez is averaging 20.5 points and nine rebounds. The four former Heat players have already become the largest part of the Bucks’ offense. 123.9 Milwaukee has allowed 123.9 points per 100 possessions through two games, the NBA’s second-worst defensive rating entering Saturday. The Bucks have surrendered 130 points per game despite their opponents shooting only 18 for 73 from three-point range, the fourth-lowest opponent rate in the sport. Washington and Chicago combined to make 24.7 percent of their threes. Milwaukee has shot 39.1 percent from deep and made 16 more three-pointers than its opponents, giving the Bucks a 48-point advantage from behind the arc. They have still been outscored by 19 points. The difference has come closer to the basket and at the foul line. Plus-42 and minus-25 The Sixers have outscored their opponents 121-79 after halftime. Their plus-42 second-half margin allowed them to erase a four-point halftime deficit against New York and a 24-point halftime deficit against Cleveland. Milwaukee has moved in the other direction. The Bucks led at halftime in both games but have been outscored 148-123 during the second half. They have lost the two fourth quarters by a combined 24 points. The way Philadelphia rallied against Cleveland also lines up with Milwaukee’s early defensive issues. The Sixers scored 69 points in the second half Thursday. They scored 36 in the paint, went 18 for 22 from the foul line and committed only two turnovers. They did that while making only three of their 13 three-point attempts. The Sixers did not need a hot shooting half to come back. They protected the ball, reached the lane and drew fouls. 66 Milwaukee has allowed 66 paint points per game, the worst mark through two contests. Washington outscored the Bucks 70-50 in the paint during the season opener. Chicago followed with a 62-44 advantage Friday. That leaves Milwaukee with a minus-38 paint differential. The Sixers scored 64 paint points against a Cleveland frontcourt featuring Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. Thirty-six came after halftime, when Philadelphia scored 69 points and turned a 24-point deficit into an eight-point victory. Milwaukee starts Turner and brings the 7-foot Ware off its bench. That size has not prevented opponents from consistently reaching the paint. Maxey, Brown and James all give the Sixers ways to attack off the dribble. Embiid presents another interior challenge if Philadelphia can deliver him the ball without repeating the turnover problems from Thursday’s first half. 71 Washington and Chicago attempted 71 free throws against Milwaukee. The Bucks committed 32 fouls against the Wizards, who went 32 for 41 from the line. Milwaukee committed another 27 fouls Friday as Chicago made 28 of 30 attempts. The Bucks have been outscored 60-33 at the foul line. They have allowed 22 more attempts and made only 67.3 percent of their own free throws. Philadelphia has attempted 57 free throws through two games. The Sixers took 22 during the second half of their comeback against Cleveland. The Bucks have allowed opponents to score 132 points in the paint and make 60 free throws. Those two areas have accounted for 192 of the 260 points Milwaukee has surrendered. 72:48 Milwaukee gave first- and second-year players only 318 minutes during the entire 2025-26 season, the lowest total in the NBA. Every other team gave that group more than 1,300. The Bucks have already distributed 72 minutes and 48 seconds to first- and second-year players through two games. Second-year guard Jakučionis has played 48:56. Rookie guard Brayden Burries has logged 23:52. They are the only Milwaukee players in their first two seasons who have appeared. Their combined total is already 22.9 percent of Milwaukee’s full-season figure from last year. That does not mean the same rate will continue over 82 games. It does show the immediate difference between a roster built around Antetokounmpo and one beginning to evaluate its younger players. The Bucks’ roster is new. The clearest place for the Sixers to attack is not. Philadelphia scored 69 second-half points Thursday by getting inside and reaching the foul line. Milwaukee has spent its first two games allowing both.

stories.detailText: Sixers rule James out for matchup with Bucks originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James will sit out for the first time as a Sixer on Saturday night. The 2-0 Sixers downgraded James’ status from questionable to out Saturday afternoon before their meeting with the 0-2 Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena. James’ official listing on the injury report was “low back/sciatica management.” Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction), Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) and Tacko Fall (left quadriceps strain) were also listed as out. Dean Wade remained questionable as of Saturday afternoon with a left ankle sprain. The night off for the 41-year-old James does not come as a surprise. The Sixers will finish their first back-to-back of the season Sunday when they host the Pistons. The team hasn’t detailed its exact plans with James and Joel Embiid’s availability, but the Sixers have made it clear that neither star will be every-game players this season. Embiid said he expects to play one leg of the back-to-back, so it appears he’ll be out Sunday. “We have plenty of meetings and discussions about it. … It’s obviously an important topic,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said on Sept. 29. “Like our fans and like all of us, we want those two guys ready to go come April.” James averaged 33.5 minutes over the Sixers’ first two games and posted 15.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 2.0 steals per contest.

stories.title: Jayson Tatum insists 'there's no beef' with Jaylen Brown in wake of trade
stories.summary: Jayson Tatum spent most of his postgame news conference addressing speculation about his relationship with former Celtics teammate Jaylen Brown in the wake of Brown's shocking trade to Philadelphia over the summer.
stories.detailText: BOSTON -- There have been rings and failures, innuendos, rumors and internet emojis, and finally, a trade that ended the Jayson Tatum - Jaylen Brown partnership in Boston . Tatum spent most of his postgame news conference Friday night addressing the social media stir that Brown created earlier this week. Brown posted a blue hat -- a symbol for "cap," the slang definition of someone being untruthful -- on Instagram in response to Tatum saying in a video on his YouTube channel that he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by Brown's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers this summer. Asked if he had any response to Brown's social media comment, Tatum sighed before expressing his frustrations with the entire situation for several minutes. "I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him," Tatum said after the Celtics' 107-103 win over the New York Knicks in Boston's home opener. "The frustrating part is since he's not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning the championship, how we've grown together, right?" Brown was drafted in 2016, Tatum a year later. Together, they helped the Celtics to a Finals win over the Dallas Maverick in 2024 along with another Finals appearance in 2022 and the Eastern Conference finals in five of eight years. Whenever the Celtics underachieved in the playoffs, there were rumors about their relationship and speculation over whether the Celtics would trade one over the other. At times, the partnership felt awkward, but Tatum believes so much has been sensationalized. "This ain't no f---ing Shaq and Kobe," Tatum said, referring to the highly publicized issues Shaquille O'Neal and the late Kobe Bryant had during their eight years together on the Los Angeles Lakers . "There's no beef. It's not about that. It should be more praise. I understand drama gets clicks and views, but I'm not really into that. I'm not blaming everybody for how they feel. Everybody is entitled to their own feelings, and we all go through different things in our lives." Tatum repeatedly pointed out that he's a father of two, and multiple times he cited a breakdown in communication, saying a conversation shouldn't be had over social media. "I reached out to him the day he was traded. I called, I texted," Tatum said. "I understand people process things differently. At this point in our lives, we're too old to be having our relationship discussed on the internet. If there's a conversation to be had, we can definitely have the conversation. "I welcome that. I've always wanted the best for him, wished the best for him. I've always publicly said those things." Much was made of the 76ers-Celtics preseason matchup in Boston in early October, where it appeared the two didn't interact during pregame warmups. The two teams meet again Nov. 10 in Philadelphia. "I've seen all these things about 'Get your popcorn ready when they play' -- like this ain't no f---ing boxing match, it's basketball," Tatum said. "I hate the conversation, the narrative around it. There's not enough communication, and a conversation will solve or put out a lot of fires." Both players made All-Star teams and had multiple All-NBA selections. Brown was named Finals MVP in 2024 by a 7-4 margin in voting, and Tatum went to the Olympic Games that summer in France -- although he didn't play much -- while Brown didn't. Tatum's 36 points, nine rebounds and seven assists Friday marked his best game since Game 4 of the Eastern Conference semifinals two years ago against the Knicks, when he scored 42 before rupturing his right Achilles, an injury that forced him to miss most of last season. With Tatum out, Brown helped carry the Celtics to 56 wins and the No. 2 seed in the East. Tatum returned for the final 16 regular-season contests and played in six games in Boston's first-round series against Philadelphia, missing Game 7 with left knee stiffness. Despite the loss, Brown called it the most fun he has had in a season. He was then traded to the 76ers in a July blockbuster that ended his 10-year tenure in Boston and brought Paul George to the Celtics. It's been one thing after another since, and Tatum hopes direct contact can put an end to the speculation. "Just a conversation. Not a bad one or anything like that," Tatum said. "Right, wrong, you can understand the other side. It's not done enough, especially in our business." Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

teamStories.detailText: AUSTIN, TX - OCTOBER 23: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs plays defense during the game against Kevin Durant #7 of the Houston Rockets during the game on October 23, 2026 at the Moody Center in Austin, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Garrett Ellwood/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Isn’t it great when your mood depends on the performance of your favorite team? It’s not a feeling I’ve experienced since abandoning fandom at school, but I empathize with those that do because the emotions and time they give a team matter. I even saw it up close with my mother recently, who has become a WNBA fan out of nowhere, and her spirits improved when her beloved Atlanta Dream got back in the win column in the Finals. Fortunately for those who have suffered this, there are no “statements” in an opener and the first weeks of the season are filled with weirdness with some teams taking long to get settled and some of the bad ones briefly performing above expectation. This means it might take a team like the San Antonio Spurs some time to reach sixth gear because they are getting creative with a three-guard set in the starting unit and they don’t have a high level of urgency at all times, so nobody needs to overreact to some speed bumps. Anyways, the logistical casualty that caused us to wait three nights for the Spurs’ second game offered some time to watch the other teams and the Oklahoma City Thunder came up again in their winning effort against the Denver Nuggets on Thursday. There was a need to see if they could follow up their opening win by making another high-quality team look as ordinary as they did the Spurs, and for the most part, they did. The Houston Rockets got checked out, too, and they looked mighty against the Dallas Mavericks. Some of the new swag was obvious when they played the Spurs because using another connector like Fred VanVleet added juice to the offense, but some of the extra intensity of the game was caused naturally by the matchup and its history. The battle for Texas supremacy is serious business and that was why the rebounding in the trenches looked like a mosh pit at times. The team was down 10 points late in the third quarter, but never let the game get out of reach while not playing their style. As much as I am a fan of playing fast, the court was like a speedway in the third quarter, which will greatly diminish anyone’s legs, even if they have a fast set of wheels. So, there’s no surprise some players were slow to make defensive reads in the fourth quarter- one example was Wembanyama not switching onto Kevin Durant when he made the handoff triple in the last few minutes. The priority always has to be protecting the 3-point line late in a close game and that was an easy enough switch. The Rockets led 89 percent of the night and upstaged the Spurs, yet it was some top-notch NBA action in large part because big-man battles, when done right, are maybe the best the league has to offer from a matchup standpoint. It’s super early in the season, but I feel ashamed for underestimating the Rockets because Durant’s length gave Stephon Castle problems and Jabari Smith Jr. was equally impactful as an off-ball defender. I’m already eager for the next matchup on Jan. 26 in San Antonio to see how the Spurs get their lick back. Wish I could report to the fans that things will be easier for the Spurs, but it seems like they’ll only have three easier games — two against the Sacramento Kings and one versus the Chicago Bulls — in the next 18 days. Takeaways: Yes, an 0-2 record is hideous, but trust me on this, things could be so much worse, like how they look for the Miami Heat. They looked a class below both the Minnesota Timberwolves and Detroit Pistons on opening week and Kaseya Center got sacked on both nights. Spurs fans would be shook up if they saw the same lack of effort and cohesion. Castle should keep working on his ball handling like he did this summer, but the 3-point shooting needs to come around soon. Opponents think so little of him from long range that they keep giving him those shots, and he needs to drain them to prevent his teammates from being schemed by an extra help defender. Yet if he loses his confidence shooting from deep, an adjustment that can be made is parking him in the dunker spot; he has the hops to be effective there and it would force his defender to play him closer. Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie are nice shooters, but there is still a need for them to be more assertive when playing next to Harper, De’Aaron Fox and Victor Wembanyama. Obviously, there are some things to straighten out if this three-guard set is going to be permanent, but in Champagnie’s case, there should never be a world where he only takes five shots when he is ignitable like jet fuel. Luckily for Wembanyama, I won’t charge for this advice, but he should remember the importance of added strength training and having post moves. Going to the body is the only way the big guys can offset his length, and think about how Şengün was collapsing the defense with post ups and was scoring. Improving in the post would give Wemby more angles to pass to his teammates, and it can also be a way to leverage a turn-around jumper. Houston’s frontline having three scoring threats and a fourth on the glass (Tari Eason will) be problematic in future matchups with the Spurs because Wembanyama can only do so much. It’s not ideal, but the next time Houston goes huge, I’d like to see what he can do sharing the court with Luke Kornet. There are plenty of moments that Houston had three of those guys together, and one figures they wouldn’t be as effective if the counter was a two-man zone with Wembanyama up front and Kornet in the back. Amen Thompson’s block on Wembanyama was spectacular, and I won’t forget it all season. Thompson and his twin, Ausar, have impressive springs in their legs and there may not be anyone who gets off the ground quicker than them in the league.

stories.title: Eagles' DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks out vs. Cowboys
stories.summary: The Eagles' top two receivers -- DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks -- have been ruled out of Monday night's game against the Cowboys.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles ' top two receivers -- DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks -- have been ruled out of Monday night's game against the Dallas Cowboys . Smith has been dealing with hamstring issues since the summer, when he was sidelined for a portion of training camp. He tweaked his hamstring Week 2 against the Tennessee Titans , saying recently that he thought being dehydrated in the Nashville heat was a contributing factor. He played through the injury the following week but missed the next two games before returning last Sunday against the Carolina Panthers , catching seven balls for 75 yards and a touchdown. Smith was unable to practice this week. Wicks appeared on the practice report this week with an ankle injury. This will be the first time he'll miss a game with the Eagles. Tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) expects to play despite missing the first two days of practice this week. The Eagles' offense could also welcome back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and lineman Landon Dickerson (knee/pec), both of whom are questionable. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been ruled out, while fellow edge rusher Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is questionable, telling reporters Friday that he is a game-time decision.

stories.detailText: Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in. Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. **UPDATED AS OF SATURDAY, OCTOBER 24 AT 5:15 PM ET** AFC East ◆ Buffalo Bills DJ Moore - WR (shoulder) Moore aggravated his shoulder injury in Week 4 and was forced from the game, unable to return. He did not play in Week 5 or Week 6. Impact: The team's Week 7 bye should afford Moore the requisite time to heal and return to the active roster when the Bills take on the Ravens on the road. Moore would be an upside WR3, if active. ◆ Miami Dolphins De’Von Achane - RB (knee) Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season. Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright . The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season. Caleb Douglas - WR (ankle) Douglas missed his third consecutive game in Week 5. The team's Week 6 bye should have afforded him enough time to return for Week 7 against the Jets. He is day-to-day and practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday . he was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Jets. Impact: Douglas demonstrated splash play potential for one of the youngest offenses in the league and could return to FLEX status once healthy. Malik Willis - QB (right thumb) Willis is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets, but received treatment on his injured throwing-hand thumb . Impact: Apparently, none. Hopefully, we get more news as the week progresses. ◆ New England Patriots Mack Hollins - WR (calf) Hollins departed the team's Week 4 win over the Bills with a calf injury and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve in Week 5. Impact: Veteran practice squad call-up Efton Chism saw the biggest increase in routes following Hollins' departure, which was particularly interesting considering the team's general lack of downfield abilities. Perhaps Kyle Williams could finally see additional time on the field. Romeo Doubs - WR (shoulder) Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined. ◆ New York Jets Breece Hall - RB (quadriceps) Hall suffered a quadriceps injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Lions. Head coach Aaron Glenn reiterated Hall remains week-to-week early in Week 6 . He finished Week 7 preparation with consecutive limited showings, drawing the questionable tag against the Dolphins. Impact: Braelon Allen can be started as a volume-driven RB2 for as long as Hall remains sidelined. Adonai Mitchell - WR (finger) Mitchell reportedly injured his finger during Week 3's Thursday practice. He returned to practice in Week 7, in a limited capacity , but was removed from the injury report Friday . He will play against the Dolphins. Impact: Mitchell's return marks the first game since Week 1 with all three of Garrett Wilson, Mitchell, and rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq fully healthy. That isn't necessarily a boost to any of them in what is now a much more crowded aerial offense. AFC North ◆ Baltimore Ravens Lamar Jackson - QB (ankle) Jackson has been out since injuring his ankle in Week 4. He practiced in a limited capacity to begin Week 7 but was ruled out Saturday. Impact: Although wide receiver Zay Flowers remains a WR, his true ceiling inarguably takes a hit with Tyler Huntley under center. Huntley grabs another start with Jackson inactive. Rashod Bateman - WR (shoulder) Bateman handled just 17 offensive snaps in the team's Week 6 loss to the Browns. Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Bateman "should be fine." He was limited to begin Week 7. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Bengals. Impact: Minimal. Durham Smythe - TE (Achilles) Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done. Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role. ◆ Cincinnati Bengals Andrei Iosivas - WR (thumb) The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3 Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable. ◆ Cleveland Browns KC Concepcion - WR (calf/quad) Concepcion was limited to begin Week 7 but removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: Concepcion cleared the NFL's concussion protocol in time to play in Week 6, but he now must rehab two leg injuries. The talented, yet banged-up rookie is on track to face the Titans, but he is stuck in the FLEX tier for now. Denzel Boston - WR (foot) Boston played through his foot injury last week and remains limited early in Week 7 . He was removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: Boston turned in an unusable stat line a week ago but appears to have avoided a significant injury. Dylan Sampson - RB (knee) Sampson was placed on injured reserve in Week 2. The Browns activated him from injured reserve Saturday and he will play in Week 7. Impact : Sampson should be rostered in 12-team formats. He could handle a sizable role if Judkins, explained below, is unable to play. Should Judkins take the field, Sampson may be able to return PPR FLEX value, and eventually earn a larger role. Quinshon Judkins - RB (ankle) Judkins resumed practicing in a limited capacity early in Week 7 after missing Week 6 with an ankle injury initially suffered in Week 5. He was removede from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 7. Impact: Both Judkins and Sampson are in the FLEX conversation, though Judkins has run inefficiently this season. Raheim Sanders - RB (hip) The Browns placed Sanders on injured reserve in Week 6 . Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed. ◆ Pittsburgh Steelers Rico Dowdle - RB (knee) Dowdle was limited to begin Week 7 and drew a questionable tag for Week 7. Impact: Dowdle returned in Week 6 but suffered an additional injury, this time finding himself questionable with a knee ailment. Fantasy managers will want to track his status when the team announces inactives early Sunday morning. Michael Pittman - WR (foot) Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice . It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5 . Impact: Pittman's absence opens the door for additional opportunities behind DK Metcalf , a role that now appears to be on rookie Germie Bernard 's shoulders following the multi-week injury suffered by Roman Wilson in Week 5. Ben Skowronek ( leg ) has already been ruled out for Week 6. Bernard is one of Week 6's top waiver additions after leading the team with nine targets against the Colts. Roman Wilson - WR (finger) Wilson departed in the second half of Week 5 with a finger injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-game absence. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: See above. AFC South ◆ Houston Texans Tank Dell - WR (knee) Dell is expected to make his season debut in Week 7 against the Giants. He was activated from injured reserve Saturday. Impact: Dell will make his first appearance since Week 16 of 2024 and is likely to be eased back into the fold after such a long time off. Fantasy managers can continue to stash him for the second half of the season. David Montgomery - RB (groin) Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Montgomery is " week-to-week " with a groin injury. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday, and remains sidelined to begin Week 7 . The team ruled him o ut for Week 7 Friday. Impact: The expected multi-game absence leaves Woody Marks atop the backfield depth chart. He is a viable FLEX starter, but the Texans showed in Week 6 that they will continue splitting backfield touches. Jawhar Jordan - RB (undisclosed) The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7 . Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined. Dalton Schultz - TE (quad) Schultz was seen limping in Week 6 and did not practice the following Wednesday . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Giants. Impact: None. Jayden Higgins - WR (knee) Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp. Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6. ◆ Indianapolis Colts Alec Pierce - WR (heel) Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said Pierce won’t practice this week. Impact: Josh Downs should serve as the primary option through the air for as long as Pierce remains sidelined. The team signed veteran field-stretcher Darius Slayton in the wake of Pierce's injury, although he is unlikely to return weekly fantasy production. Slayton (knee) was ruled out for Week 5 on Friday. Tyler Warren - TE (groin) Warren was added to the team's injury report on Friday and was designated questionable for Week 6. He did not play against the Titans and remains sidelined early in Week 7, before being ruled out Friday. Impact: An absence leaves the Colts without one of their top playmakers, filtering additional volume to Keenan Allen , Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor , though Taylor is the bankable fantasy football asset. ◆ Jacksonville Jaguars The Jaguars emerged from their Week 6 loss to the Texans absent any fantasy-relevant injuries. ◆ Tennessee Titans Calvin Ridley - WR (hip) Ridley was limited on Wednesday and drew the questionable tag for Week 7. Impact: Removing him from the lineup would benefit the Titans' young wide receivers. Tyjae Spear - RB (knee) Spears is listed as questionable in what seems like a weekly occurrence. Impact: Likely none. AFC West ◆ Denver Broncos Pat Bryant - WR (ankle) Bryant suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 loss to the 49ers and is reportedly expected to miss "a few weeks." He was placed on injured reserve Friday. Impact: Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims appear to be the next men up in Bryant's absence, although the team could use a "sum of all parts" mentality to bridge his absence, considering historical trends. Alpha wide receiver Jaylen Waddle would be the primary beneficiary. Jonah Coleman - RB (ankle) The team shocked fantasy managers Saturday, sending him to short-term injured reserve in late September. He was activated from injured reserve Saturday and will play against the Cardinals. Impact: Coleman began his takeover of the backfield in Week 2 before going down with an injury that sent him to injured reserve. Considering how poorly veteran J.K. Dobbins has performed in his absence, expect Coleman to immediately be reinserted as the primary ball carrier in a plus matchup, making him worthy of a start as a FLEX option in plus matchup against the Cardinals. Jaylen Waddle - WR (chest) Waddle was limited to begin Week 7. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Cardinals. Impact: Waddle is struggling to perform, stuck in the Broncos' unproductive offense. His chest injury will not impact his availability, but he is best treated as a WR3/FLEX. ◆ Kansas City Chiefs Rashee Rice - WR (hamstring) Rice departed Week 4 with a hamstring injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-week absence. He missed Week 6 and remains sidelined early in Week 7, before being ruled out for Sunday Night Football against the Seahawks. Impact: Wide receivers Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong have received increased playing time, though neither is doing much with it. Once-intriguing rookie Cyrus Allen appears to be an afterthought. Travis Kelce - TE (ankle) Kelce played through the ankle injury last week. He was limited on Wednesday but removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: None. Tyquan Thornton - WR (ankle) Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks. Impact: See above. ◆ Las Vegas Raiders Brock Bowers - TE (hamstring/calf) Bowers was limited on Wednesday but removed from the injury report Friday . Impact: These are new injuries for Bowers. We do not know whether he suffered them in-game in Week 6 or during practice on Wednesday. Mike Washington Jr. - RB (back/foot) Washington was limited on Wednesday and drew the questionable tag for Week 7. Impact: Like Bowers, we do not know when these injuries occurred. Ashton Jeanty would further consolidate touches if Washington misses time. Dont’e Thornton - WR (hamstring) The Raiders are still waiting for Thornton to " show " something as he enters his third and final practice week in his 21-day practice window. Impact: Thornton could carve out a role as a deep threat, once healthy, but can only be viewed as a dart throw. Jack Bech - WR (forearm) The Raiders placed Bech on injured reserve in Week 4. Impact : Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker could line up in the slot more often. ◆ Los Angeles Chargers Ladd McConkey - WR (concussion) McConkey was forced from the team's Week 6 loss to the Chiefs due to a concussion after just eight offensive snaps. Impact: McConkey appears likely to avoid missing time with the head injury considering the team heads to its bye in Week 7. Expect McConkey back on the field for Week 8 against the Rams. Tre' Harris - WR (hamstring) Harris missed the team's Week 6 loss to the Chiefs with a hamstring injury. Impact: Harris could return following the team's Week 7 bye. David Njoku - TE (fibula) Njoku is looking at an extended absence after being carted from the field in the team's Week 2 loss to the Raiders. The Chargers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . Impact: See above. NFC East ◆ Dallas Cowboys Malik Davis - RB (hip) Davis was placed on injured reserve and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams . Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1 in Week 2. ◆ New York Giants Jaxson Dart - QB (knee) Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. He will undergo surgery to address the MCL and meniscus and miss the rest of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely. Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was benched in favor of recent acquisition J.J. McCarthy in the second half of their loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed McCarthy as the starter for Week 7. ◆ Philadelphia Eagles Saquon Barkley - RB (hamstring) The veteran workhorse pulled up lame in the second quarter of Week 4 and is reportedly considered "week-to-week." He did not play in Week 5 but the team is reportedly " hopeful " to get back their franchise back for Week 6. After not playing in Week 6, Barkley drew the questionable tag for Monday Night Football in Week 7 against the Cowboys. Impact: Primary backup Tank Bigsby also departed the team's Week 4 loss to the Rams, leaving with a core muscle injury that requires surgery. He was placed on injured reserve Monday. Running back Will Shipley suffered an injury in Week 5. The Philadelphia backfield is currently a mess. DeVonta Smith - WR (hamstring) Smith was ruled out for Week 7 Saturday. Impact: As was fellow receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) , leaving the Eagles with four heathy receivers on the active roster. Tight end Dallas Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences, returning a tidy TE1 profile in a plus matchup against the Cowboys. Tank Bigsby - RB (core) See above. Impact: See above. Jalen Hurts - QB (blood clots) Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. He was ruled out for Week 6 and could be looking at an extended absence. He was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after more clots were found in his lungs. Impact: Hurts is currently sidelined indefinitely. Tanner McKee enters the starting lineup under center following the release of Andy Dalton. The Philadelphia offense could be in trouble in the immediate future considering the sheer number of injuries. Will Shipley - RB (foot) Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot in Week 5. He is expected to miss multiple weeks. Impact: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are the only healthy backs currently on the roster, assuming Saquon Barkley misses another week. Neither are overly exciting streaming options, although we would prioritize Pierce. ◆ Washington Commanders Terry McLaurin - WR (knee) McLaurin suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in Week 6. Impact: Treylon Burks should step into primary perimeter snaps, although he suffered an apparent injury late in the fourth quarter. No update has been passed on Burks as of Tuesday. Stefon Diggs will likely serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver moving forward. Marcus Mariota - QB (knee) Mariota departed the team's Week 4 loss in London with a sprained MCL , leaving Athan Kaliakmanis as the likely backup, for the time being. Mariota remained sidelined in Week 5 and was ruled out for Week 6. Impact: None. Jaylin Lane - WR (ankle) Lane suffered a dislocated ankle and fracture in Week 4 and is likely done for the season. Impact: Minimal. Lane was primarily a special teams contributor. Jacory Croskey-Merritt - RB (groin) Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice this week and ruled out for Week 6 against the 49ers. The team placed him on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: Expect Rachaad White to fill in as the primary rusher, with Austin Ekeler on hand to soak up primary change of pace duties. White can be started as a viable FLEX option while Ekeler is likely best left on fantasy benches. NFC North ◆ Chicago Bears Kyle Monangai - RB (thumb/toe) Head coach Ben Johnson labeled Monangai as " day-to-day " with a thumb injury suffered in Week 4, but he was later revealed to have suffered a turf toe injury as well. He remains sidelined for the Bears' Week 7 game against the Patriots on Thursday . Impact: D'Andre Swift is splitting touches with Roschon Johnson . Swift is RB2-viable, while Johnson can be started in the FLEX. Cole Kmet - TE (knee) Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team's Thursday Night Football win over the Patriots. Impact: Expect Sam Roush to serve as the team's TE2 for the remainder of the season, while second-year tight end Colston Loveland should continue his recent ascension back into TE1 territory. ◆ Detroit Lions Isiah Pacheco - RB (back) Pacheco was placed on injured reserve to start the season. General Manager Brad Holmes said he "hopes Pacheco returns this season." Impact: Well, that doesn't sound great. There appears to be something more insidious going on with Pacheco's back than initially thought. Lions coach Dan Campbell said running backs Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could split touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs . Saylors appears to be the first player up. Gibbs handled an absurd 34 opportunities, of 37 total running back opportunities, in the team's Week 1, overtime win over the Saints ◆ Green Bay Packers Christian Watson - WR (ankle) Watson was limited on Wednesday . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Lions. Impact: We do not expect this to impact Watson's availability. Matthew Golden - WR (shoulder) Golden was limited on Wednesday . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Lions. Impact: None. Jordan Love - QB (back) Love was limited on Wednesday . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Lions. Impact: Love should be good to go for Week 7, though ideally he upgrades to full participation on Thursday. Jayden Reed - WR (neck) Reed suffered a scary-looking neck injury that required stabilization in the team's Week 2 win over the Jets. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday that it is " way too early " to determine whether Reed will play again in 2026. That said, he was not placed on injured reserve ahead of their Week 3 contest. He will reportedly undergo surgery . Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are likely to soak up additional snaps, although volume is most likely to concentrate on Christian Watson , Matthew Golden , and Tucker Kraft . Chris Brooks - RB (ankle) Brooks suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 win over the Buccaneers and is reportedly undergoing further testing. He did not play in Week 5 or Week 6. Impact: Brooks had been the most consistent rusher in a timeshare situation. Kaleb Johnson lost another fumble in Week 4, leaving MarShawn Lloyd as the likely beneficiary for as long as Brooks remains sidelined, although that role carries little value for the team with the fewest rush attempts in the league through the first month of the season. Skyy Moore - WR (ankle) Moore sported a walking boot instead of practicing on Wednesday . He was ruled out for Week 6 Friday . Impact: Should he miss time, the Packers' star players would further consolidate touches. ◆ Minnesota Vikings Jordan Addison - WR (hamstring) Addison did not play in Week 5. Coming off the Week 6 bye, he is practicing in full for Week 7 . Impact: Addison returns to the FLEX category for the Vikings' game against the Colts. Jordan Mason - RB (thumb) The Vikings placed Mason on injured reserve in Week 2 . The team reportedly “ hopes ” to get him back in Week 7. He was activated from injured reserve Saturday and will play in Week 7. Impact: Mason should return to the lead rushing role this week. T.J. Hockenson - TE (concussion) Hockenson sustained a concussion in Week 5. He is practicing in full coming off the Week 6 bye. Impact: He is a TE1. Justin Jefferson - WR (ankle) Jefferson was limited on Wednesday . Impact: None. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. NFC South ◆ Atlanta Falcons Brian Robinson - RB (hamstring) Robinson was limited on Wednesday before missing practice Thursday and Friday. He was ruled out for Week 7 Friday. Impact: This directly benefits lead back Bijan Robinson , who typically cedes meaningful touch counts to Robinson. ◆ Carolina Panthers Bryce Young - QB (knee) Young is practicing in full . Impact: None Jonathan Brooks - RB (groin) Brooks aggravated the groin injury that forced him to miss the end of camp. The Panthers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. He is expected to undergo core muscle surgery . Impact: Chuba Hubbard enters the volume-driven RB1 discussion in Brooks' absence. Trevor Etienne ( ankle ) is practicing in full and can be stashed in 14-team leagues, while AJ Dillon was ruled out. ◆ New Orleans Saints Travis Etienne - RB (hamstring) Etienne aggravated his hamstring injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Raiders. Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that he expects Etienne to "miss some time." Impact: Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller appear likely to split the load in Etienne's absence, neither of whom is overly enticing in fantasy circles in what is expected to be a shared workload. Jordyn Tyson - WR (hamstring) Tyson begins the regular season on injured reserve . He reportedly traveled with the team to Paris for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, but will not begin practicing this week . Impact: Tyson is trending toward returning following the Saints' Week 8 bye. Alvin Kamara - RB (back) Kamara and CJ Donaldson ( shoulder ) were limited on Wednesday . Both were removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Paris in Week 7. Impact: This is a banged-up, ineffective committee. Buying low on Travis Etienne (hamstring) makes sense. ◆ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Jalen McMillan - WR (knee) McMillan suffered a sprained PCL in his first game action of the season in Week 3. The team placed him on injured reserve Monday, with an expected absence of 6-8 weeks. Impact: Not much change considering he made his season debut in Week 3, although rookie Ted Hurst should remain in the starting lineup. Baker Mayfield - QB (thumb) Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb in the team's Week 3 loss to the Vikings. He is practicing fully in Week 7 and appears ready to return . Impact: Mayfield is a high-end QB2 if active. His presence would stabilize the offense. Bucky Irving - RB (illness) Irving did not practice on Wednesday but was removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: Likely none, but this is worth monitoring. Sean Tucker (quad) is practicing in full. Emeka Egbuka - WR (foot/concussion) Egbuka did not practice on Wednesday. He was ruled out for Week 7 Friday. Impact: Wide receivers Chris Godwin (eight) and Ted Hurst (six) trailed Egbuka in targets (16) last week and are in line to benefit from Egbuka's absence. Tight end Cade Otton could also see additional volume over the middle of the field. NFC West ◆ Arizona Cardinals Jeremiyah Love - RB (ankle) Love was sidelined throughout Week 6 and remains sidelined early in Week 7 . The team lists him with just one ankle injury despite recent reports indicating that his preseason ankle injury remains problematic and he injured his other ankle in Week 4. He was ruled out for Week 7 Friday. Impact: Tyler Allgeier was outplayed by Bam Knight in Week 6. This would likely be a committee in Week 7 if Love remains sidelined. ◆ Los Angeles Rams Terrance Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson aggravated an ankle injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Broncos and was sent to injured reserve . As of Week 7, he needs more rehab time . Impact: Colby Parkinson (shoulder) is playing through his injury and Davis Allen (foot) is sidelined. Tyler Higbee is a viable TE1/2 in fantasy, though he was outplayed by Parkinson in Week 6. Davante Adams - WR (hamstring) The Rams placed Adams on i njured reserve with a ruptured hamstring tendon. He is expected to miss 6-10 weeks, though as of Wednesday in Week 7, the team has not yet scheduled his required procedure, clouding his recovery timeline. Impact: Puka Nacua should see all the volume he can handle in the absence of Adams, while a shift to heavier rates of 12- and 13-personnel is likely in store for the Rams as they fight through another significant injury. Tyler Higbee suddenly finds himself a fantasy TE1, at least until Ferguson returns, while Nacua challenges for overall WR1. A recent ESPN report indicates the Rams will explore the trade market, though head coach Sean McVay denies it . Adams could be replaced as the team's No. 2 wide receiver while injured. Trading him away now could pay off. Puka Nacua - WR (calf) Nacua was added to the injury report Thursday with a new ailment, did not practice Friday, and is listed as questionable for Week 7. Impact: About as big as there is in fantasy, honestly. Nacua has been utterly dominant whenever Adams has been off the field, but now appears in legitimate danger of missing Week 7. Furthermore, the timing of the game places fantasy managers in a pickle considering the game kicks off in the afternoon portion of the Sunday slate, meaning those that are more risk averse would want to begin alternate plans now. We likely won't know Nacua's status until the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to kickoff. Expect heavy rates of 13-personnel regardless of Nacua's status, which could turn into the team's new base alignment if Nacua is unable to go. ◆ San Francisco 49ers Christian Kirk - WR (calf) The 49ers activated Kirk's 21-day practice window. He is practicing in full for Week 7 but drew the questionable tag. Impact: Kirk has a chance to become the 49ers' de facto No. 1 wide receiver in the short term. Mike Evans - WR (Achilles) Evans aggravated his Achilles injury in Week 6 and is expected to " miss some time ." He was ruled out for Week 7 Friday. Impact: The hits to the San Francisco pass catchers continue as Evans now appears to be in line to miss at least Week 7. The team has its bye in Week 8, potentially setting up a situation where Evans misses only one contest. Expect volume to concentrate on Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle, with the team also expected to be without Deebo Samue l for their game against the Falcons. As you can see below, there are now five wide receivers unavailable for the 49ers. Demarcus Robinson - WR (ankle) Robinson suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team's Week 2 win over the Dolphins. He will miss significant time. Impact : Reports suggest Jacob Cowing will be leaned on to fill the void left behind by the injuries to Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling . Expect Mike Evans , assuming health, Christian McCaffrey , and George Kittle to soak up additional volume. Deebo Samuel - WR (hamstring) Samuel suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 5 win over the Seahawks. He is expected to miss multiple weeks and was ruled out for Week 7 Friday. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Brandin Cooks is the "next man up" for a 49ers team absolutely devastated by injuries. Cooks can be added from waivers after serving as the de facto WR2 opposite Mike Evans once Samuel departed. De’Zhaun Stribling - WR (ankle) Stribling suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 1 win over the Rams. The 49ers placed him on injured reserve in Week 2 after he underwent surgery to repair a deltoid ligament tear. He is expected to return in 10 weeks. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Demarcus Robinson will be the primary beneficiary. Ricky Pearsall - WR (knee) Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve. Impact: Pearsall will miss the entirety of the 2026 season. ◆ Seattle Seahawks Zach Charbonnet - RB (knee) Charbonnet reportedly has a " legitimate chance " to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs, and is now practicing in full . That said, the team ruled him out Friday . Impact: Fantasy managers will have to wait another week for the return of Charbonnet, who should not be on waivers. Rashid Shaheed - WR (hip) Shaheed was limited on Wednesday but removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: None. Shaheed is only relevant in 14-team leagues. Jadarian Price - RB (chest) Price was placed on injured reserve in Week 4. Impact: Price played through the injury in Week 3 but apparently emerged worse off for wear. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani will split the backfield in his absence, although the biggest boost likely falls back to Jaxon Smith-Njigba .

stories.title: Giants roster moves: Tremaine Edmunds to IR, Paulson Adebo returns
stories.summary: Giants shuffle roster as more injuries hit the defense; Jalin Hyatt elevated from practice squad.
stories.detailText: Tremaine Edmunds | Getty Images The New York Giants continue to take hits on defense. The Giants have placed inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, the team’s leading tackler through six games, on injured reserve with a torn chest muscle. The Giants also announced on Saturday that starting safety Jevon Holland, who has a team-high three interceptions, has been downgraded to out with a concussion. Edmunds had 50 tackles in six games. He was second behind rookie Arvell Reese in solo tackles with 34. Micah McFadden, a full-time starter at linebacker for the Giants in 2023 and 2024, will take Edmunds’ place. McFadden played in just one game last season due to a foot injury. The Giants have also lost edge defender Brian Burns, who has 16.5 sacks in 2025, and starting defensive lineman Chauncey Golston for the season. To take Edmunds’ place on the roster, the Giants are activating veteran cornerback Paulson Adebo from injured reserve. Adebo played in just one game before going on IR with a knee injury. He could start on Sunday against the Houston Texans as Greg Newsome II has already been ruled out with a concussion. The Giants also announced that tight end Theo Johnson will miss a second straight game with a neck injury. He had initially been listed as questionable. Chance for Jalin Hyatt Wide receiver Jalin Hyatt was one of two practice squad elevations for the Giants. The other was safety Raheem Layne. Hyatt, a 2023 third-round pick by the Giants, has been on the practice squad all season. He has 36 receptions in 41 career games. Layne gives the Giants protection if Tyler Nubin (neck) can’t play.

stories.title: Packers activate RB Josh Jacobs for 2026 debut
stories.summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs will make his 2026 season debut against the Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL's commissioner exempt list.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs will make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the Detroit Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL's commissioner exempt list. Green Bay added him to the active roster from exempt status Saturday. The NFL took Jacobs off the exempt list Monday. The NFL's investigation of Jacobs for potential violations of the personal conduct policy following his arrest earlier this year on misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor destruction of property charges remains active, and a suspension could be equal to or greater than the number of games he already missed. The six games he has missed would be credited toward any suspension. For now, Jacobs is cleared to play. Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to the charges resulting from the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and reached a deferred judgment agreement on the property damage charge. Without Jacobs, the Packers have had the worst running game in the NFL, ranking last in rushing yards per game at 59.8 yards. Jacobs was the Packers' leading rusher the previous two seasons, ranking eighth in the league in combined rushing yards (2,258) and tied for fourth in rushing touchdowns (28) during the 2024 and 2025 seasons. The Packers also signed WR/KR Coleman Owen to the active roster off the practice squad, elevated edge rusher Arron Mosby from the practice squad for game day, and activated defensive tackle Jordon Riley off the physically unable to perform list.

stories.title: 49ers activate WR Christian Kirk from IR
stories.summary: The 49ers made a procedural move on Friday, releasing defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to make room for wide receiver Christian Kirk.
stories.detailText: The 49ers made a procedural move on Friday, releasing defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to make room for wide receiver Christian Kirk. They made things official Saturday. The 49ers activated Kirk from injured reserve to the active roster, and they re-signed Okoronkwo to the practice squad. Okoronkwo and linebacker Jalen Graham were elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Falcons. The team cut defensive lineman Kevin Givens from the practice squad. Kirk has spent the season on injured reserve. He signed a one-year deal with the 49ers in free agency in March and will help Sunday in Mike Evans' absence. The team's top wide receiver was ruled out with Achilles soreness. Kirk, a second-round pick of the Cardinals in 2018, has 432 receptions for 5,415 yards and 30 touchdowns in eight seasons. Okoronkwo, 31, has appeared in all six games with one start this season. He has two tackles and a sack.

stories.title: Best content of the week: Lions CB Rakestraw eager to build on success
stories.summary: Will Burchfield of 97.1 wrote about how Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. is ready to play in a big divisional game.
stories.detailText: It wasn’t exactly a storybook beginning for Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. Be it injuries, bad luck, or a combination of both, he never really had the opportunity to get his NFL career going. However, the past is the past, and Rakestraw, now in his third year in the NFL, has put together a string of solid performances. Will Burchfield of 97.1 has the story on how Rakestraw is happy to be moving in the right direction , but aware that he has more work to do in order to solidify his status as a full-time starter on the Lions’ defense. “I just gotta worry about myself,” Rakestraw said to Burchfield. “If they go get a corner, they go get a corner. stories.title: Ravens discussion: who will step up after Tavius Robinson’s injury?
stories.summary: The Baltimore Ravens will be counting on their young outside linebacker depth to step up after Tavius Robinson’s season-ending pectoral injury. The fourth-year defender occupied a 72% defensive snap share to start the season (46.6 per game) while also contributing to the kick return, punt return, and field goal block …
stories.detailText: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Zion Young #9 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will be counting on their young outside linebacker depth to step up after Tavius Robinson’s season-ending pectoral injury. The fourth-year defender occupied a 72% defensive snap share to start the season (46.6 per game) while also contributing to the kick return, punt return, and field goal block teams. He leads the defense with 3.5 sacks and the edge rusher room with 18 tackles, leaving a sizable void to be filled. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s take on replacing Robinson: Nikhil Mehta Rookies Zion Young and Ethan Burke have the physical profile to step up in Robinson’s absence, but more than anything, the Ravens need Mike Green to figure out how to rush the passer off the left side of the defense. He spent plenty of time there in college, but has lined up on the blind side more often in Baltimore with better splits. Based on his film, he’s still getting the feel for transitioning from his explosive first step into his pass rush moves. Green clearly has the athleticism and skillset to make it work, but he has to do so quickly. If not, Eric DeCosta may have to scour the trade market for another edge rusher who can win on third down. Zach Canter The Ravens have a big role to fill with Tavius Robinson going down for the season. T-Rob was an every down player, setting the edge, getting to the quarterback and capable of sliding inside with power. While Ethan Burke has done well in his limited action and more is expected to come, and Kaimon Rucker and Adisa Isaac could get snaps of the practice squad, the best answer is Zion Young. Young presents a very similar play style to Robinson, an excellent edge setter with grown-man NFL play strength to be able to slide inside. While he hasn’t shown the pass rush chops like Robinson, who has 3.5 sacks in 6 games, Young will be the first, next man up and get the biggest uptick in snaps. The real answer will be the Ravens trading for Khalil Mack, but we’ll have to see if the Ravens can play themselves into a spot to justify a move like that at the deadline. Dustin Cox The Ravens will need their second-round rookie, Zion Young, to step up and help to fill the role left behind by Tavius Robinson. Young’s profile is similar to Robinson’s, as both are power rushers who are strong run defenders on the edge. The rookie will likely have to take on a lot more snaps than originally envisioned, but throwing him into the deep end now could hopefully produce results for the talented linebacker sooner rather than later. Baltimore will likely need to add another body to the mix, whether that be via a practice squad call up, free agency, or through a trade before the deadline, but Young is the most obvious replacement on the current roster. Now, it’s your turn! Which Raven are you expecting to step up after Tavius Robinson’s injury? Let us know in the comments section below!

stories.summary: The Vikings activated running back Jordan Mason from injured reserve Saturday, completing his recovery from a fractured thumb that required surgery last month.
stories.detailText: EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings activated running back Jordan Mason from injured reserve Saturday, completing his recovery from a fractured thumb that required surgery last month. The Vikings had already created a spot for Mason on the 53-man roster Friday by releasing running back DeeJay Dallas , who re-signed Saturday to the Vikings' practice squad and was elevated to the gameday roster for Sunday's matchup against the Indianapolis Colts . Mason is expected to split time against the Indianapolis Colts with teammate Aaron Jones Sr ., who took 90% of the Vikings' running back carries in Mason's absence. "Getting Jordan back, I think will be a really positive thing just because of the offseason he had and the excitement," coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday, after Mason completed a week of practice with no setbacks. "My excitement to see him paired with Aaron, and how we go about the usage there, is going to be an exciting thing because we feel so confident in both of them. But with the workload Aaron's had and the type of warrior he's been, it'll be good to have JP back." In his only appearance this season, Mason carried 15 times for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 39-22 victory over the Green Bay Packers . He reported thumb soreness the following day, leading to the discovery of a small fracture. In his second season with the Vikings, Mason has rushed for 2,070 yards and 14 touchdowns since joining the San Francisco 49ers in 2022.

stories.title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson (ankle) vs. Bengals; Tyler 'Snoop' Huntley to start
stories.summary: The Baltimore Ravens have ruled QB Lamar Jackson out of Sundays game vs. the Cincinnati Bengals as he continues to deal with a high ankle sprain. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley will get the start.
stories.detailText: BALTIMORE -- The Baltimore Ravens ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals , which means the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will miss his third straight game. On Saturday, the Ravens downgraded Jackson, who had been listed as questionable with a high left ankle injury after being limited all week in practice. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley , who is 6-8 as a fill-in starter for the Ravens, will replace Jackson in an early critical AFC North game for Baltimore. After a disappointing loss at the Cleveland Browns last Sunday, the Ravens are looking to avoid falling to 0-2 in the division for the first time in 19 years. After Friday's practice, Jackson didn't look like a quarterback who was close to full strength, limping to the lectern for his media session. He was also not seen as players walked off the field Friday, which suggests he did not finish practice. Jackson said Friday that he was "heading in the right direction" and the decision would come down to pain tolerance. "If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play," Jackson said. "But if I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and get hit, that's not helping my team at all." Jackson injured his ankle on the last offensive snap before halftime in a win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. It looked like Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson II 's shoulder landed on the outside of Jackson's left ankle, which caused it to bend awkwardly. In returning to practice this week, Jackson acknowledged it hurts when he tries to run and plant his foot. "It's just like trying to run ... can't put too much pressure [on the left foot]," Jackson said. This month, Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 12 before struggling in a 13-10 loss at the Browns on Sunday. The Ravens' offense has lacked consistency without Jackson. In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 10 quarters with Huntley, Baltimore has totaled 40 points and four touchdowns. This marks the second straight season in which Jackson has missed multiple games due to injury. Last season, he missed three straight games due to a hurt hamstring. On Friday, he expressed regret rushing back from it because he was never truly healthy the rest of last season. "I feel like that was dumb a little bit because I was still hurting," Jackson said. "I'm trying to help my team win, but I'm not to my full capability or not even close to it." The loss of Jackson is a significant one for Sunday's game between the Ravens (4-2) and Bengals (3-2). Since 2019, the Ravens are 0-3, including the playoffs, against the Bengals without Jackson as their starting quarterback.

stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Malachi Toney #1 of the Miami Hurricanes and Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrate a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Panthers during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The University of Miami honored the 2001 national championship team on Saturday. And the 2026 version proved that imitation is the best form of flattery by flattening the Pitt Panthers 52-23 wearing those 2001 throwback jerseys (which looked incredible). Malachi Toney was a man among boys, setting a school record with 16 catches that he turned into 194 yards and three touchdowns. Darian Mensah was 31/37 for 387 yards and four touchdowns with no turnovers. Javian Mallory led all rushers with 7 carries for 47 yards and two touchdowns. Miami opened with a near perfect start, forcing a quick punt and driving into the Pitt red zone. A touchdown run by Mark Fletcher, Jr. was called back for a hold on Gavin Mueller, and after a sack, Miami settled for a field goal and a 3-0 lead. The Hurricanes’ defense was excellent in the first half though, forcing punts on the following three drives. Over that span, Miami added touchdowns to cap off 41- and 78-yard touchdown drives. Toney took a screen on an overloaded side and trotted for an easy 19-yard score and a 10-0 lead. The next drive, Mallory took what looked to be a short run up the middle and cut to the right and to the end zone for a 16-yard touchdown and a 17-0 lead. Miami was in position to really blow the doors off the game quickly and went for it on fourth-and-1. Mensah had about three receivers open, including in the flat for an easy dump off and big gain. But he fired deep down the field to an open Daylyn Upshaw, who dropped it. Pitt would turn around and go 55 yards on six plays and draw to within 17-7 on a five-yard touchdown run by Damon Ferguson, Jr. Miami would answer with a 75-yard scoring drive. Toney, who left for a while getting what appeared to be his ankle tended to, returned, and he took a short pass through the Pitt defense for a 53-yard touchdown and a 24-7 lead. On the next Pitt play, JJ Dunnigan punched out the ball from Pitt QB Holden Geriner, and Justin Scott recovered. Mensah found Mueller for his first career TD on a tiptoe catch near the sideline for a 31-7 lead. Pitt would complete a Hail Mary (which is becoming a big problem), and the receiver would get dragged down at the half yard line to end the first half. Miami would get the ball first in the second half after Pat Narduzzi called for an onside kick which Miami recovered. A 44-yard catch by Vandrevius Jacobs led to a two-yard Fletcher run, and this game was in the bag at 38-7. Pitt would go on their own scoring drive the next time up, with Cataurus Hicks beating Ethan O’Connor for a 36-yard touchdown. But Miami would go up 45-14 on a methodical 11-play drive that ended with Mallory bowling into the end zone from two yards. Mensah connected with Toney early in the fourth quarter from 11 yards to put Miami up 52-14 and end the day for a number of starters. Pitt got a safety and backup QB Corey Dailey threw a 49-yard touchdown pass with less than a minute left to end the scoring. A dominant day for the No. 1 team in the land.

stories.title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders have unionized
stories.summary: One of the NFL's teams has another union to deal with — and the team in question didn't fight it.
stories.detailText: One of the NFL's teams has another union to deal with — and the team in question didn't fight it. Via the Associated Press, the Dallas Cowboys have agreed to recognize the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association as the collective bargaining representative for the team's cheerleading squad. "The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for the talent and dedication they exhibit," the union said in a statement. "They remain one of the most sought-after opportunities for talented dancers worldwide." Employers typically prefer to avoid unions, for obvious reasons. Through collective bargaining and the ability to strike, unions can secure better pay and better working conditions for all employees in the bargaining unit. The Buffalo Jills were the first NFL cheerleading squad to unionize, back in 1995. The Jills disbanded in 2014 after the filing of a lawsuit alleging violations of the New York minimum-wage laws. Questions about fair pay for NFL cheerleaders have been common over the years, along with allegations of improper conduct. The Washington franchise, while under the management of Daniel Snyder, faced civil claims arising from a " secret outtake " video. Those claims were later settled . In 2022, longtime Cowboys P.R. executive Rich Dalrymple abruptly resigned amid allegations that he secretly recorded the team's cheerleaders while they were changing clothes. Four cheerleaders received $2.4 million to settle their civil claims as a result of that incident.
